repos/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418.body:
## Problem Statement

Sandcastle picks its own work, and it does one item at a time.

`.sandcastle/workflows/sequential-reviewer/implement-prompt.md:5` hands the implementer a `gh issue list` of the whole `ready-for-agent` queue and `:29–38` hands it a priority heuristic — bug fixes → tracer bullets → polish → refactors — for choosing among them. So the maintainer cannot say *work on this SPEC*: they can only say *how many issues*, and an agent decides which. Four defects follow, each silent:

- **Work selection is an agent's read of prose.** The four heuristic categories were never labels. Nothing computes them, nothing asserts them, and the run's own record of what it chose is a transcript.
- **A `blocked_by`-chained SPEC cannot be drained.** [ADR-0010](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/blob/main/docs/adr/0010-sandcastle-workflows-are-folders-driven-by-injected-dispatch.md)'s loop stops on the first dispatch that produces no commits, and its comment reads *"the backlog is empty or everything left is blocked"* — one conflation of two facts. The previous SPEC's eight slices each carried `total_blocked_by: 1`, so a scoped run would have resolved to one eligible descendant, drained it, and stopped. Eight slices, eight launches.
- **`docs/agents/triage-labels.md:24` promises something no code does.** *"The Sandcastle runner adds `code-review` to a SPEC when every released slice is closed."* There is no `gh issue edit` anywhere in `.sandcastle/`. `main.mts:31` is a bare `All done.`
- **A sequential implement→review loop is too slow on a large SPEC.** Ten slices at ten to fifteen minutes per dispatch pair is a two-hour run in which one machine with ten cores runs one agent. [#406](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/406) measured the ceiling: build throughput at three concurrent worktrees is **1.67×**.

A fifth defect is structural and was found while designing the fix. ADR-0010 claims *"`DispatchOptions` omits `sandbox`, `branchStrategy`, `maxIterations` and `hooks` so no workflow can contradict ADR-0001."* `Dispatch` returns Sandcastle's `RunResult`, whose `resume?`/`fork?` options type omits none of `branchStrategy`, `cwd` or `hooks` — so this compiles today in `sequential-reviewer/workflow.mts`:

```ts
const implement = await dispatch(IMPLEMENTER, { promptFile: "implement-prompt.md" });
await implement.resume?.("keep going", { branchStrategy: { type: "merge-to-head" }, hooks: {} });
```

A second agent iteration, on a branch strategy ADR-0001 forbids, with hooks the runner never chose. Nobody has written it — but *cannot be written* was the claim.

And a sixth, in the opposite direction: `runner.mts:31–33` hardcodes `swift package resolve`. The runner already knows this is a Swift repo, which is the one thing it must not know if Sandcastle is to drive a web or mobile repo.

## Solution

Give the **runner** Work scope and the **driver** the loop.

**Work scope is universal runner input, selected before Workflow.** Three choices in picker order — **Specific SPEC**, **Specific issue**, **All ready-for-agent issues** — resolved over GitHub into a frozen, version-pinned snapshot, flattened into an ordered work list, and truncated by a run guard, all before any workflow exists. A workflow cannot read `scopeKind`, cannot see dependency edges, and cannot name a work item: it declares a **driver** and supplies one item's implement→review **body**, reached through a `dispatch` already scoped to that item.

**A third workflow runs waves.** The **wave-parallel** driver cuts a host worktree per work item from the workspace branch's tip, dispatches a whole wave concurrently, merges every settled branch back with `git merge --no-ff` in run order, and cuts the next wave from the updated tip. A **Planner** agent may subset the current ready level and nothing else; a **Merger** agent verifies the merged tree once per settled wave. The run still never pushes and never opens a pull request — the maintainer reviews one Conductor branch, exactly as today.

**The layout**, as ADR-0010's amended Layout section already records it:

```
.sandcastle/
  main.mts                      pick → prepare → drive → print error
  runner.mts                    preflight → memoise providers → RunCore; hands off to a driver
  contract.mts                  Agent, Workflow, WorkflowContext, Dispatch, DispatchOptions, DispatchResult
  repo.mts                      the only per-repo module: hooks, copyToWorktree, MAX_PARALLEL default, item timeout
  scope/snapshot.mts            pure: WorkScope, WorkScopeSnapshot, eligibility, ordering, levels, digest
  scope/github.mts              the only module that talks to GitHub
  drivers/registry.mts          DRIVERS, keyed by id
  drivers/{sequential,wave-parallel,whole-branch}.mts
  drivers/outcomes.mts          pure: skip set, merge order, Merger skip, the settle predicate
  drivers/ledger.mts            pure: itemLine, the append-only renderer, the heartbeat
  agents/catalog.mts            IMPLEMENTER, REVIEWER, PLANNER, MERGER
  cli/{flow,prompts,store}.mts  the picker, its clack adapter, the run store
  workflows/registry.mts        WORKFLOWS, in picker order
  workflows/sequential-reviewer/{workflow.mts, implement-prompt.md, review-prompt.md}
  workflows/wave-parallel/{workflow.mts, implement-prompt.md, review-prompt.md, plan-prompt.md, merge-prompt.md}
  workflows/review-only/{workflow.mts, review-prompt.md}
```

**`contract.mts` becomes an allow-list.** `DispatchOptions` is two keys — `promptFile`, `promptArgs?` — and `DispatchResult` is two fields — `commits`, `baseSha`. Across both shipped workflows that is the entire use of `RunOptions` and `RunResult`, so the module stops exporting a Sandcastle type at all, and the `resume`/`fork` hole closes because an allow-list cannot be defeated by a return type.

**Everything repo-shaped moves to `.sandcastle/repo.mts`** under one rule: *the runner may run a command whose output it discards; it may never run a command whose exit code it branches on, git excepted.* A pre-warm is fire-and-forget. A verify's exit code must be interpreted and repaired, which is judgment — so the verify loop stays in `merge-prompt.md`, and dropping Sandcastle into the web repo is one file to edit plus whatever prompts differ.

## User Stories

1. As a maintainer, I want to name the SPEC a run should work through, so that an agent never chooses what to work on.
2. As a maintainer, I want a run to accept a bare issue number or a GitHub issue URL, so that I can paste from the browser.
3. As a maintainer, I want a closed, blocked, unreleased or `ready-for-human` target refused at the prompt with its number, title and labels shown, so that a bad target costs one screen rather than an hour.
4. As a maintainer running a `blocked_by`-chained SPEC, I want the chain to *order* the work rather than exclude it, so that ten chained slices are one run instead of ten launches.
5. As a maintainer, I want a dependency cycle in a SPEC refused before confirmation, so that a run never deadlocks on its own ordering.
6. As a maintainer, I want the confirmation to read `up to 10 of 30 eligible`, so that a partially drained SPEC is stated rather than implied.
7. As a maintainer, I want one 1–50 guard on how many work items an unattended run may drain, whatever scope I chose, so that an overnight run cannot burn my whole token budget.
8. As a maintainer, I want the run to work three items at once in their own worktrees, so that a ten-slice SPEC finishes in one evening.
9. As a maintainer, I want a Planner that can keep two items which rewrite the same module out of the same wave, so that concurrency does not manufacture merge conflicts the dependency edges cannot express.
10. As a maintainer, I want a Planner that can never invent, widen or reorder work, so that adding a planning agent does not hand work selection back to a model.
11. As a maintainer, I want each item's reviewer to see only that item's commits, so that a long run does not re-review work that already passed.
12. As a maintainer, I want one `--no-ff` merge commit per merged item on my workspace branch, so that an otherwise flat ten-item diff still tells me which change belongs to which issue.
13. As a maintainer, I want the merged combination verified once per wave, so that a rename in one item that breaks another item's call site is caught by the run rather than by me in the morning.
14. As a maintainer, I want an item that produced no commits to skip its dependents transitively, so that slice 4 is never implemented on slice 3's missing foundation.
15. As a maintainer, I want a bounced item to merge and its dependents to run, so that one unmet criterion does not cancel most of a SPEC.
16. As a maintainer, I want a hung item bounded by a wall-clock timeout and reported as `timed out`, distinctly from a failing suite, so that a deadlock is never recorded as evidence about the work.
17. As a maintainer, I want an item whose issue was closed while its work never merged reopened with a comment naming its branch, so that GitHub never claims work that lives on an abandoned branch.
18. As a maintainer, I want a merged item's worktree and branch deleted and an unmerged one's kept, with no force flag anywhere, so that git itself refuses to destroy work.
19. As a maintainer, I want a leftover `sandcastle/*` branch or worktree to refuse the next run, so that a machine never guesses about half-finished work.
20. As a maintainer returning after ninety minutes, I want a scrollback I can read top to bottom, so that I learn what happened rather than what is happening.
21. As a maintainer watching a wave, I want to be able to tell a slow item from a wedged one, so that I know thirty minutes before its timeout does.
22. As a maintainer, I want a drained SPEC labelled `code-review` and never closed, so that the judgment `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` promises is made by the runner and the one it does not is made by me.
23. As a maintainer, I want the run's own report never to re-enter a later run's prompt, so that the fifth run of one SPEC does not read four previous reports as evidence.
24. As a maintainer, I want the run's target pre-filled from my last run only in the worktree that chose it, so that a Conductor workspace never starts an unattended run against a SPEC it has nothing to do with.
25. As a maintainer, I want to drop `.sandcastle/` into my web repo and edit one file, so that Sandcastle is not a Swift tool.
26. As a maintainer, I want a new execution shape to be a new driver rather than a wider contract, so that extending Sandcastle never means letting a workflow reach further.

## Implementation Decisions

Every decision below is settled on a closed ticket of [map #389](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/389); the ticket holds the reasoning and the rejected alternatives. **Read the linked ticket before changing a decision in a slice.** ADR-0001 and ADR-0010 are already amended in place on `main` ([#414](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/pull/414)) and are the second authority.

### The snapshot and eligibility — [#390](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/390)

- **A version-pinned REST snapshot, built by the runner before any dispatch.** Pin `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` and `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10`; paginate everything. Read `/issues/{n}`, `/issues/{n}/sub_issues` recursively, `/issues/{n}/comments`, `/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocked_by`.
- **Parse the target locally.** A bare positive integer or an exact same-repository `/issues/<number>` URL; build the API path from the fixed repository plus the parsed number; reject a pull request or a mismatched canonical repository/number. **`gh issue view --repo` is not a safe resolver** — a live probe showed a URL overriding `--repo`.
- **Traverse the whole tree before filtering**, through closed, blocked, unreleased and `ready-for-human` intermediates. `blocked` derives only from blockers whose current state is `open`, because `/blocked_by` returns closed relationships too.
- **The frozen snapshot** carries `schemaVersion`, `repository`, `scopeKind`, `anchorNodeId`, `memberNodeIds`, `executableNodeIds`, normalized `issues` with exclusion reasons, and `snapshotId`, a SHA-256 over canonical JSON. Kind literals are **kebab-case** (`specific-spec`, `specific-issue`, `all-ready-for-agent`).
- **Fail closed.** `404` surfaces as "not found or inaccessible" without pretending to distinguish them; a cross-repository or partial tree aborts scope loading; any auth, permission, rate-limit, pagination or comment-page failure aborts before dispatch. **An API failure is never an empty list.**
- **Revalidate the current item and its ancestry immediately before each dispatch.** A mismatch never dispatches stale or newly ineligible work.
- This is **structural and auditable scope control, not a security boundary**: ADR-0001 puts agents on the host with the maintainer's `gh` login.

### Ordering, stop conditions and handoff — [#394](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/394)

- **An in-scope open blocker is a precedence edge, not an exclusion.** Membership stays frozen; a blocker that is itself in the eligible set *orders* its dependent instead of removing it. Only a blocker outside the set still excludes. A **dependency cycle aborts before confirmation.** This is what makes waves exist.
- **The work list is a stable topological sort keyed on authored sub-issue order** — depth-first pre-order over each parent's `childNodeIds`, so a slice's own children precede the next sibling. The repository-wide queue has no parent, so it tie-breaks on **ascending issue number**. Authored order is the one signal carrying maintainer intent, because GitHub's reprioritise endpoint edits it.
- **Truncation is a prefix of that order and is applied after the sort**, so the guard can never hand over an item whose blocker was cut.
- **`implement-prompt.md:29–38`'s priority heuristic is deleted** along with its query, and **is not handed to the Planner.** So is `:75`'s *"leave a comment on the issue and move on"* — an agent handed one item has nowhere to move on to.
- **Every stop condition turns on: does the foundation exist?** Zero commits → skip the item **and every in-set item `blocked_by` it, transitively**; independent items still run. A bounce → the code landed and was judged incomplete, so the run continues **including dependents**. **A skip never backfills** — item 11 is not promoted when item 3 is skipped.
- **The runner owns the skip set; a workflow never receives dependency edges.**
- **Mid-run drift, by cause:** item closed → skip the item, continue with dependents; item deregulated (`ready-for-agent` removed, `ready-for-human` added, newly blocked from outside the set) → skip transitively; **anchor** changed (closed, or lost `spec`/`ready-for-agent`) → **abort the run** before dispatch. **Membership is never refreshed. No skip is ever silent.**
- **Handoff:** at end of run, re-read the anchor's descendants from **live GitHub state** and add `code-review` when the anchor is **open**, carries `spec`, and **every `ready-for-agent` descendant is closed**. **The runner never closes a SPEC.** An aborted run reports and labels nothing.
- **The report** goes to stdout on every run and additionally as **one comment on the anchor**, opening with the fixed marker `<!-- sandcastle-run-report -->`. **Comment normalization drops any comment carrying that marker**, so the run's own bookkeeping never re-enters a later prompt. Item-level bounce comments are untouched. The repository-wide scope gets **no durable report** — there is no anchor.

### The contract — [#392](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/392), superseded on its shape by [#405](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/405)

- **The contract describes a driver, not a list.** There is no `work: readonly WorkItem[]` and no `work` key on `DispatchOptions`. `WorkItem` leaves `contract.mts` entirely. The guarantee strengthens: *"a dispatch that names no work item does not compile"* becomes *"a dispatch cannot name a work item at all; the driver decided which one before the body ran."*
- **What survives from #392, on its own reasoning:** the runner owns Work scope; all three kinds are flattened before any workflow sees them; a workflow cannot read `scopeKind`; a workflow cannot forge a work item; the runner writes every scope prompt arg; the pre-dispatch revalidation; the universal run guard; `Knob`'s death; the `scope/` module split; the `ResolveScope` picker seam.
- **The two contract types, in full:**

```ts
export interface DispatchResult {
  readonly commits: readonly { readonly sha: string }[];
  readonly baseSha: string;
}

export interface DispatchOptions {
  readonly promptFile: string;
  readonly promptArgs?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
}
```

  Decided by arithmetic: across both shipped workflows the entire use of `RunResult` is `commits.length` and `baseSha`, and the entire use of `RunOptions` is `promptFile` and `promptArgs`. It is also the **only** shape both `run()` and `Worktree.run()` can satisfy. **`stdout` stops crossing the seam** — a workflow that can read agent stdout can branch on model output.
- **The body:**

```ts
await core.runWaves(async (item, dispatch) => {
  const implement = await dispatch(IMPLEMENTER, { promptFile: "implement-prompt.md" });
  if (!implement.commits.length) return;
  await dispatch(REVIEWER, {
    promptFile: "review-prompt.md",
    promptArgs: { REVIEW_BASE: implement.baseSha },
  });
});
```

- **Drivers are the extension point, and capability is strictly non-increasing.** A workflow declares a driver and receives the context *that driver* grants. `sequential` (one item at a time, host checkout), `wave-parallel` (a wave at a time, per-item worktree, Planner + Merger), `whole-branch` (no work items). Extending means **reusing a driver, never reaching further**. `drainsWorkItems` is **deleted** — draining and concurrency are driver properties the picker reads.
- **No worktree handle ever crosses the seam.** Sandcastle's `Worktree` carries `.close()`, `.createSandbox()` and `.interactive()`.
- **Outcomes never reach the contract.** The body returns `void`; the driver reads git, the process and GitHub, never the workflow's testimony:

| Outcome | How the driver knows |
| --- | --- |
| committed / no commits | `git rev-list <waveBase>..sandcastle/<n>-<slug>` |
| crashed | the body's promise rejected — `allSettled` caught it |
| timed out | the driver's own `AbortSignal` fired |
| bounced | re-read the issue from live GitHub when the item settles |
| merged / conflict-rewound | `git merge --no-ff`'s exit code |

  **Outcomes are two-phase:** `LoopOutcome = committed | no-commits | crashed | timed-out`, then `MergeOutcome = merged | conflict-rewound | skipped-upstream` for committed items only. **A bounce is an annotation on a committed item, never an outcome.**
- **`prepare(plan)` returns the runner core**, and `DRIVERS[plan.workflow.driver](core, plan.workflow)` cannot be invoked without a value only a passing preflight produces. The preflight: every distinct model's CLI version and login (shipped), `gh auth status`, a clean workspace tree, no leftover `sandcastle/*` branch or worktree, and the frozen ordered list. **Levels stay unfrozen** — they are a pure function of `(list, accumulated skip set)`, recomputed at each wave boundary, because a transitive skip shrinks what is ready.
- **ADR-0010's *"the loop is the workflow's `for`"* becomes:** *there is exactly one loop over work items per run, and it belongs to the driver. A workflow supplies that loop's body; it can neither create a loop nor bound one.* Sandcastle's own iteration stays pinned at 1 on both paths.
- Who supplies what the omissions used to name: `branchStrategy: { type: "branch" }` — the wave-parallel driver, to `createWorktree`; per-worktree hooks — repo config → driver; `sandbox: noSandbox()` — the driver, **explicitly, because `WorktreeRunOptions.sandbox` is required and does not default**; `maxIterations` — nobody.

### Repo-shaped configuration — [#405](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/405) §6

```ts
export const repo: RepoConfig = {
  onHostReady:        [{ command: "swift package resolve" }],
  onWorktreeReady:    [{ command: "swift package resolve" }, { command: "swift build --build-tests" }],
  copyToWorktree:     [],   // cloning `.build` breaks the build on an absolute PCH module-cache path
  maxParallelDefault: 3,    // #406: throughput peaks at N=3 and inverts at N=4
  itemTimeout:        { minutes: 45 },  // provisional; a real run calibrates it from per-item durations
};
```

> **The runner may run a command whose output it discards. It may never run a command whose exit code it branches on — except git's, which is framework-neutral.**

Rejected: JSON or TOML (loses typed defaults, gains a parser); per workflow folder (wrong axis — `swift package resolve` is a fact about this repo, not about Implement & Review).

### The picker and the store — [#391](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/391), [#393](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/393), [#403](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/403) §5

- **The walk:** Work scope → target → **resolve** → fast path → workflow → run guard → `MAX_PARALLEL` → models/effort → confirm.
- **`cli/flow.mts` stays pure, synchronous and spawn-free.** Resolution is injected, following the `EffortsFor` precedent: `export type ResolveScope = (scope: WorkScope) => Promise<ScopeOutcome>`. The flow gains a third step kind so the *point at which* resolution happens stays inside the pure module — `Question` becomes `Step`, `nextQuestion` becomes `nextStep`, and `ResolveStep` carries `scope`, `needsTarget` and `initialValue`.
- **A failed resolution returns the recovery select:** retry GitHub, enter another target, choose another Work scope, cancel. Cancellation is safe at every prompt.
- **The confirmation's Work scope and Eligible rows belong to `cli/flow.mts`, not `runShape`** — which is what keeps `runShape` down to one number and the anchor out of the workflow. `runShape: (workItems: number) => string`, e.g. `plan → implement → review, waves of up to 3, up to 10 issues`.
- **The run guard is universal**: asked whenever the driver drains and **more than one** work item is eligible. 1–50, default 10. Specific issue never asks.
- **`MAX_PARALLEL` is a picker question**, asked only when the driver runs items concurrently, defaulted from `repo.mts`. Chosen over a constant because contention depends on what the Mac is doing right now, which only the human at the keyboard knows.
- **The store remembers answers, never outcomes.** Stored: `lastWorkflowId`, `lastScope: { kind, target, origin }`, `maxWorkItems`, `maxParallel`, `agents`. Never stored: the snapshot, `snapshotId`, any wave plan, completed/bounced/skipped records, the run report, the anchor's title.
- **Work scope is pre-fill, not replay.** The remembered kind and target become the scope question's `initialValue`, and the fast path moves to **after** resolution. Three properties follow: the fast path's hint can state eligibility, accepting it always starts a run, and **staleness needs no representation** — a stale target fails in place and lands in the existing recovery paths.
- **`lastScope.origin` gates the target only.** `git rev-parse --git-dir`, a free sibling of the `--git-common-dir` call `runStorePath` already makes. `kind` always pre-fills; `target` pre-fills only in the worktree that wrote it, because the store lives in the git common dir and every Conductor workspace is a different piece of work.
- **Schema stays version 2 and gains top-level passthrough.** `parseStoredRun` today drops unrecognised top-level keys and `serializeStoredRun` never re-emits them, which would erase the new fields from an old branch and erase `knobs` from a new one. Carrying unknown top-level keys through absorbs the orphaned `knobs` key **with no special case**, and extends key-level upsert from ids to fields. **A version bump is the worst option here** — an old parser fails `version !== 2`, treats the store as empty and destroys the agent picks too.
- **`knobs.maxIterations` is not migrated into `maxWorkItems`.** They are different parameters that happen to both be integers.
- **`storeIsReplayable` gains two clauses:** a remembered **draining** workflow additionally requires `maxWorkItems`; a remembered **concurrent** workflow additionally requires `maxParallel`. The fast path vanishes for exactly one run after upgrade and the next write fills the key in.

### The Planner — [#403](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/403), amended by [#405](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/405)

- **The Planner is a level splitter.** It is handed the current ready level and may only **subset** it. It cannot discover work, add an item, widen a wave, cross a level, name a branch or reach past the resolved Work scope. Its one real power is **co-scheduling risk** — two ready items that rewrite the same module — which the dependency edges do not encode.
- **Wave size *is* concurrency; there is no semaphore.** A semaphore would silently undo the Planner's only power: two items it separated could still overlap while it drains a wide plan. A too-wide plan is a validation failure, not something quietly degraded.
- **Plan shape — numbers plus advisory deferral reasons, never titles or branches:**

```
<plan>{ "wave": [12, 15, 21],
        "deferrals": [{ "number": 18, "reason": "rewrites runner.mts, as does #12" }] }</plan>
```

  The runner supplies titles from the snapshot and **names branches deterministically**. Everything the runner already knows is a forgery surface if echoed back.
- **Validation splits in two.** Shape is the library's, via `Output.object({ tag: "plan", schema, maxRetries: 1 })`. Semantics are the runner's, applied **outside** that validator: an item outside the current ready set, more than `MAX_PARALLEL`, **zero items**, or duplicates → invalid. **Omitting ready items is legal — that is the power.**
- **A zero-item plan is invalid, not "done."** Upstream's `if (issues.length === 0) break` is its stop condition; our ready set is runner-computed and known non-empty, so an empty plan can only mean *defer everything* — a livelock.
- **An invalid plan falls back to the runner's computed wave** — the first `MAX_PARALLEL` of the ready level in settled order — with **no semantic retry and no abort**. Semantic validation must live outside the Standard Schema validator precisely so that "no semantic retry" is true rather than aspirational.
- **The fallback renders a wave-level ledger line** ([#396](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/396)). Composed with the silent prompt and the per-item-only outcomes, the Planner's failure mode was designed to be invisible: every wave could silently become the computed wave, the run completes, the ledger looks perfect, and the one genuinely new component has never worked. **Telling the human after the run is not telling the agent during it** — `plan-prompt.md` stays silent.
- **One dispatch per wave, skipped when the ready level holds exactly one item** (the only valid plan is that item). Not skipped merely because the level fits `MAX_PARALLEL` — a two-item level can still hold two items that must not run together.
- **The Planner never sees dependency edges either**, and **runs no queries**.
- **The driver dispatches the Planner** (#405 §1), and `plan-prompt.md` stays in the workflow folder, resolved against `workflow.dir`. The Planner and Merger are **not `Dispatch` calls** — they are driver-internal host dispatches, which is why they alone can use `output`.
- **There is no zod.** `.sandcastle/package.json` has two dependencies. Hand-roll the `StandardSchemaV1` validator — the interface is small and both schemas are two fields. **`maxRetries` requires provider session resume**, and `run()` fails at entry otherwise; `claude-code` and `codex` both resume, so `maxRetries: 1` is safe for every provider the registry offers.

### Topology, fan-in and cleanup — [#404](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/404)

- **There is no stack and no pull request.** Every item runs in its own host worktree branched from the workspace branch's current tip; when the wave settles the runner merges each settled branch back into that branch; the next wave's worktrees are cut from the updated tip. `prepare()` preflights a clean tree, because `git merge` refuses over uncommitted changes and finding that at wave 3 is the *auth-failure-at-iteration-7* problem.
- **`--no-ff` on every merge, in run order, not completion order.** Without it the first merge of each wave fast-forwards and that item's attribution disappears. With it, every item leaves a `Merge branch 'sandcastle/375-…'` commit — **the only per-item boundary in an otherwise flat diff.**
- **Fan-in is the runner's; verification is the prompt's.** The runner keeps only what git gives it free: merging, conflict detection from the exit code, the rewind to the pre-merge SHA, cleanup, and the per-item timeout.
- **The Merger is dispatched once per settled wave** — handed nothing, a conflicted branch, a broken tree, or both. It **never merges what git merged cleanly** and **never closes an issue** (upstream's CLOSE ISSUES section dies entirely). **Skipped when exactly one branch merged cleanly into an unmoved base**, because the merged tree is then identical to a tree that item's own loop already gated. Accepted cost: a clean multi-item wave pays one dispatch that usually runs two commands and returns — the price of the runner not knowing what language the repo is written in.
- **Failure semantics:**

| Outcome | Merged? | Dependents | Worktree/branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Settled with commits | Yes, `--no-ff` | Proceed | Deleted |
| Zero commits | No | Skipped transitively | Kept |
| Crashed (`allSettled` rejected) | No | Skipped transitively | Kept |
| **Timed out** | No | Skipped transitively | Kept |
| Conflict the Merger cannot resolve | No — rewound to the pre-merge SHA | Skipped transitively | Kept |
| Bounced (issue reopened) | **Yes** | **Proceed** | Kept |
| Merged tree fails to build after the Merger | Left as-is | — | **Run aborts** |

  **A conflict rewinds one item; a broken tree aborts the run — the asymmetry is attribution.** A conflict belongs to exactly one branch. A tree that merges cleanly and then fails to build is a semantic conflict the runner cannot attribute. **A partial wave still advances**; a wave where nothing settled leaves the tip untouched and needs no special case.
- **Branches are `sandcastle/<issue-number>-<slug>`**, slug from the snapshot title, lowercased, non-alphanumerics collapsed, truncated.
- **Cleanup is merge-gated and self-enforcing.** `git worktree remove` and `git branch -d`, and **no `--force`, `-D` or `-f` appears anywhere in the cleanup path** — git itself refuses to destroy anything unmerged, and a refusal becomes a line in the report rather than an error. A leftover branch or worktree found at `prepare()` **refuses the run**.
- **Nothing is ever auto-cleaned on abort, and there is no resume.** A dirty worktree is reported and never vetoes.
- **The reviewer still diffs `REVIEW_BASE...HEAD` inside its own worktree, before fan-in.**
- **The bounce loses its structural gate.** A bounced item's code lands on the workspace branch and nothing structurally prevents it reaching `main` when the maintainer merges. **It is a report to read, not a gate that holds** — accepted openly, because drafts are gone.

### Closed but unmerged — [#412](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/412)

- **The defect is a predicate, never an outcome:** *closed, yet nothing of this item reached the workspace branch.* The discriminator — did the implementer reach its step 6 — is exactly what the driver cannot observe, and #405 forbids asking the workflow.
- **Two acts on different keys.** **Reopen** iff `closed ∧ unmerged` (`gh issue reopen <n> --comment "…"`). **Comment** iff `commits exist ∧ unmerged`, whatever the issue's state. The split is forced by the **bounced-and-rewound** item: already open, so no reopen fires, and its branch would otherwise be named in no durable place at all.
- **Per item at settle, not in an end-of-run sweep** — a broken merged tree aborts the run, and a sweep never reaches the run that went worst.
- **Over dispatched items only**, so the run never reopens an issue a human closed mid-run — #394's drift table answers that case differently and correctly.
- **A merged-but-bounced item gets neither act.** Open claims *unfinished*, which is exactly the reviewer's ruling; it never claimed no code exists.
- **In every draining driver**, where `sequential`'s reading of *unmerged* is *zero commits* — which catches an `implement-prompt.md:68` violation neither driver could previously detect. `whole-branch` drains nothing and is untouched.
- **The comment is human-facing and carries the run-report marker**, so normalization drops it and no later agent reads it. `prepare()` guarantees a human cleared that branch before any later agent could act on the item, so **the branch it names is stale by construction**.
- **A reopen is a tracker correction, never work selection.** A reopened item is **not eligible again in the run that reopened it**, written as a rule rather than left to the skip set.
- **Payoff, self-enforcing with no coordination:** every reopen lands before the anchor's `code-review` condition is evaluated against live state, so a drained SPEC with a rewound slice correctly goes **unlabelled**.

### The prompts — [#395](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/395), [#410](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/410)

- **The achievable guarantee is that the prompt never tells the agent other work exists.** "Prove the prompt cannot query beyond scope" is **not structurally achievable** — the implementer holds `gh` because it must close its own issue.
- **One JSON promptArg, `{{WORK}}`**, carrying the snapshot record verbatim — `number`, `title`, `body`, `labels`, `comments`, plus a nested `spec` key holding the ancestor SPEC or `null`. **JSON, not markdown**, because a body containing a fenced block would break straight out of a markdown splice. `comments` is load-bearing: it is how a reopened item arrives carrying the reason it bounced.
- **The reviewer takes the same record and never re-fetches** — the live issue carries the implementer's own summary arguing its work is correct. The **`Closes #<n>` line survives as a cross-check** whose mismatch is a reportable Spec finding, which makes a wrong changelog anchor detectable for the first time.
- **Review Only's `{{ANCHOR}}` is a JSON record and the prompt branches on its own `spec` label** — so no `scopeKind` reaches the workflow. A `spec` anchor unlocks a **third Spec question nobody has ever asked**: does the branch deliver the SPEC, whose criteria no slice reviewer ever saw. `:64`'s prohibition on walking a *work item's* criteria is **kept and widened** to every slice a `Closes` line names. `{{ANCHOR}}` is **always substituted** — literal `null` under repository-wide scope, routed into the existing degradation section, renamed **When there is no anchor**. The diff range stays `origin/main...HEAD` in every scope. The `review-only/workflow.mts` comment rejecting an anchor knob as *"work selection wearing a different hat"* is **void** — delete it.
- **The blocked path forbids a token commit and stays silent on the transitive-skip cascade.** An agent told that no commit drops a whole dependency subtree has a motive to manufacture one, which corrupts #394's stop condition silently and unfalsifiably.
- **The wave-parallel implement and review prompts are byte-identical copies** of the sequential pair. Sandcastle already does everything a variant would need: `preprocessPrompt` expands shell blocks at `ctx.sandboxRepoDir`, which on the worktree path *is* the worktree; `Worktree.run()` injects `SOURCE_BRANCH`/`TARGET_BRANCH` as the item's branch and rejects any override; the agent's cwd is the worktree. **Beyond `{{WORK}}` a worktree dispatch needs no argument.** Cost: a fix applied twice, detectable as a plain file comparison.
- **The implementer is never told its siblings exist.** It is alone in its worktree and can observe nothing; `Implement only your work item` already forbids the edits that conflict; conflict cost belongs to the Merger.
- **`plan-prompt.md` takes two args** — `{{READY}}` (JSON array of `number`, `title`, `body`) and `{{MAX_PARALLEL}}` — includes no document, runs nothing, and is told the cost asymmetry outright: *a wrong deferral costs a wave; an unflagged overlap costs one merge — so when the items do not tell you they collide, put them in the wave.* Order inside `wave` is explicitly meaningless.
- **`merge-prompt.md`** takes one JSON `{{WAVE}}` (branch, pre-wave `base` SHA, `merged` with each merge commit, `unmerged` with conflicted paths), states its precondition (*the runner has already rewound each failed merge*), carries this repo's verify loop, includes the coding standards and **deliberately omits `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`** — the document that teaches `gh` has no business in the context of an agent forbidden to touch the tracker. Its section **The distinction that must not blur**: *never report a failing build as an unresolved conflict, and never abandon a branch because the tree does not build.* Repair scope: fix the integration, not the feature. Its rules: never touch the tracker, never push or open a PR, never use a force flag, never reset/rebase/delete, implement nothing.
- **The Merger reports through `<merge>` structured output** — `{ "verified": bool, "unresolved": [], "notes": "…" }` via `Output.object({ maxRetries: 1 })`. Forced, not preferred: the two-key allow-list denies a workflow body both `output` and `completionSignal`, `runner.mts` sets no completion signal at all so `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>` is inert today, and the runner may not run the command that would tell it whether the tree builds.
- **Corrections worth not rediscovering.** The `clack.text` ambush is in `interactive()`, which the runner never calls; `run()` and `Worktree.run()` **fail loudly** on a missing key, which is why two args are safe. **Prompt args cannot inject a shell block** — only the file's own blocks are marked for execution. **No per-item prompt can ever request structured output** — `WorktreeRunOptions` has no `output`.
- **Reserved prompt-arg names** written by the runner or driver: `WORK`, `ANCHOR`, `READY`, `MAX_PARALLEL`, `WAVE`. The only key a body writes is `REVIEW_BASE`. Disjoint, and at five names worth an assertion rather than a convention.
- **Prototype text to lift verbatim** — all four commits are reachable from this clone's object database; verify with `git cat-file -t <sha>` before starting a slice, and if a commit is unreachable **report it rather than reinventing the prose**:
  - `223868c` (`prototype/scope-aware-prompts-395`) — the three shipped prompts, rewritten.
  - `232f7d8` (`prototype/parallel-prompts-410`) — `.sandcastle/workflows/wave-parallel/{implement,review,plan,merge}-prompt.md`.
  - `117c787` — `.sandcastle/PROTOTYPE-wave-run-report/`, **already on `main`** via [#413](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/pull/413).
  - `t3code/wayfinder-scope-map-issue-406` — `docs/worktree-parallelism-measurements.md`, on no branch that reaches `main`.

### The run display — [#411](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/411)

- **The driver renders an append-only ledger.** Half the question dissolved on a library fact: `LoggingOption` has **two** variants at 0.12.0, not three, and `stdout` resolves to `ClackDisplay` — spinners and `taskLog`, i.e. cursor control. Three concurrent dispatches would fight over one cursor, so **concurrency forces `file` mode** and per-item log files are the only permitted shape, not a choice.
- **`file` mode is not silent.** `printFileDisplayStartup` writes two unsuppressable `console.log` lines per dispatch, arriving at moments the driver does not choose — which is why a repainting dashboard loses: it cannot own the cursor it needs, and it degrades to nothing when piped. An **AFK** run wants a scrollback, not a view of *now*.
- **`onAgentStreamEvent` exists only on the `file` variant** and is the one live per-agent signal available — in exactly the mode concurrency forces.
- **Liveness is a sparse ten-minute metronome plus a five-minute silence alarm** (~14 lines per 84-minute run), with a matching resume line. Rejected: a two-minute per-item metronome (~120 lines buries the record it lives in) and the alarm alone (a healthy run goes silent for fifteen minutes, so frozen and working look identical). The alarm flags a wedged item **thirty minutes before its timeout does**. **Elapsed renders against the item timeout**, because that is the only thing that will end a hang.
- **One `itemLine` serves the live view and the end-of-run report**, so they cannot drift, and **nothing is report-only**. Seven outcomes across two phases; **`timed out` carries its own glyph and colour and shares neither with `crashed`**; `↩ bounced` and `↻ reopened` are **composable annotations**, not one optional suffix.
- **Progress is `n/10 settled` against the frozen selection.** Membership is frozen, so a transitive skip **settles** an item rather than shrinking the total, and the fraction only grows.
- **A failure interrupts no sibling, and the display never asks a question** — there is nobody there to answer it. The log path is repeated only under an alarm or an outcome worth opening a log for (`crashed`, `timed out`, `no commits`, `conflict rewound`); an approved item never gets one.

### Testing — [#396](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/396)

**Four tiers.** Tier 1 is structural (a compile error or unreachable by construction) and is delivered by the decisions above. Tiers 2–4:

- **Tier 2, pure over hand-authored snapshot literals**, because the question under test is *does this tree of edges produce this order*, not *does GitHub's JSON look like this* — and the cycle case and the blocker-outside-the-set case cannot be recorded at all without manufacturing them on the real tracker. Split the way `resolveAgents`/`validateModels` already are: **fetching is side-effecting; everything downstream is pure over a snapshot value.** Coverage: recursive descendant discovery; eligibility filtering; single-issue isolation; the repository-wide queue; the topological sort and prefix truncation; **precedence edge vs exclusion**; cycle abort; level computation and levels shrinking under transitive skips; **plan validation** (wrong level, zero-item, over-width, unknown number, duplicate — each falling back with no retry and no abort); Review Only anchor-record construction and the `spec`-label branch; store version 2, top-level passthrough, key-level upsert, `{ kind, target, origin }` pre-fill and the origin gate; the picker walk's ordered step ids; `itemLine` for all seven outcomes in both renderings plus the fallback line; the single-item Merger skip; the closed-but-unmerged truth table.
- **Plus exactly one recorded fixture as a skippable schema canary.** Hand-authored literals share one fatal blind spot: `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` is a newer GitHub surface, and if it is renamed or nested, **every hand-authored test still passes while production sees zero blockers and dispatches a whole SPEC dependency-blind.** Tier 1 cannot catch it — our own type is the thing that is wrong. Refreshing the canary needs the network and is done deliberately, never automated.
- **Tier 2, driver-owned, against a real temp git repo with a fake body.** **You only fake what is expensive**: agents cost money, minutes and a provider login; real git costs nothing. It is also the only way to assert the three claims #404 rests on that are really claims *about git* — that `--no-ff` leaves exactly one merge commit per item, that a conflicting merge fails detectably enough to rewind one item, and above all that **`git branch -d` refuses unmerged work**, which is the entire no-force-flag safety argument. Against an injected `Git` port all three would be asserted against a fake written by the same person who wrote the assumption. **The driver takes its repo root as an explicit parameter.** Concurrency needs no real timing — a fake body returns promises resolved in a chosen order. **Accepted cost: the driver suite spawns processes and touches the filesystem, breaking the current 120-test *spawns nothing* property.**
- **Tier 3, static sweeps over source as data.** Admission rule: **a sweep enumerates from a registry or the filesystem, never from a literal list of today's cases.** This is the only tier covering code that does not exist yet, which is what *every current and future workflow* requires. Written as three hardcoded assertions about `runner.mts`, `sequential` and `wave-parallel`, "no toolchain command reaches a driver" silently stops covering the fourth driver added later — which is exactly how a framework-agnostic boundary rots while the suite stays green. **This forces a `DRIVERS` registry into existence.**
- **Tier 4: one real run, and it is the maintainer's.** Every issue in this tree is `ready-for-agent` by design — this SPEC is meant to be drained AFK — so acceptance is **not** a released slice and not a `ready-for-human` sub-issue. When the maintainer tests the finished workflow they file **one** acceptance issue and record its evidence as `docs/manual-verification/issue-<n>-*.md` in the existing eight-use format: a **Candidate** table (issue, commit, build, OS, hardware, tester, date, Result) and an **Evidence** table of state / result / observation. What that run should look at is written down under *What only a real run can prove* below, so nothing is lost by not pre-filing it.
- **Where this lives, split by lifespan.** The matrix is consumed once, here — after that the tests *are* the record. The **admission rules** constrain unwritten code forever, so they go to an ADR. Explicitly **not** `docs/TESTING.md`, which is a FoldWise Voice document; putting Sandcastle's strategy there welds a portable tool to a Swift coverage guide.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every slice below is closed, and `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` is green on the workspace branch.
- [ ] The picker asks Work scope **first**, and a run cannot start without a resolved scope.
- [ ] No `gh issue list`, no priority heuristic and no `ready-for-agent` string remains in any implement prompt.
- [ ] `contract.mts` exports no Sandcastle type, and `DispatchOptions` has exactly two keys.
- [ ] No toolchain command appears in `runner.mts` or in any module under `drivers/` — asserted by a sweep that enumerates `DRIVERS`.
- [ ] No `--force`, `-D` or `-f` appears in any driver's cleanup path — asserted by a sweep.
- [ ] Three drivers and three workflows are registered, and the sequential and Review Only workflows behave as they do today.
- [ ] Every criterion above is checkable by an agent from the branch alone. **This SPEC carries no criterion that needs a human**, by design — the one thing only a human can do is named below and is not a slice.

## What only a real run can prove

Written down here rather than pre-filed as a `ready-for-human` issue, because every issue in this tree is meant to be AFK-drainable. **When the maintainer tests the finished workflow, this is the checklist for the single acceptance issue they file.** It is not a slice, it does not gate any slice, and no agent is asked to do it.

Three claims are reachable by no automated test. **The Planner is a model** — tier 2 proves the *validator* rejects a bad plan; nothing can prove a real model produces a good one. **Concurrent worktrees** — three agents editing three worktrees cut from the same branch is a condition no unit test creates. **Fan-in on real work** — `--no-ff` merges of real, unpredictable diffs, not fixtures a test author chose.

Worth checking, in rough order of what would go undetected otherwise:

- **The Planner's plan was accepted, not fallen back to, in at least one wave** — from the wave-level ledger line, not inferred from the run completing. Its failure mode was deliberately designed to be survivable, so a run where every wave silently fell back has proven nothing about the Planner.
- `git log --merges --oneline <workspace-branch>` shows **exactly one merge commit per merged item**, each naming its issue, matching the ledger's merged count. Because merge commits are the only per-item boundary in an otherwise flat diff, this is a **complete and honest census** of what merged — falsifiable months later by anyone with the branch.
- **At least two waves ran, and wave 2 was cut from the tip after wave 1's fan-in** — verifiable from wave 2's items' base SHAs.
- **Each item's reviewer saw only that item's commits**, from `REVIEW_BASE` in that item's transcript. Never verified on this repo, and now load-bearing in three places.
- **A review demonstrably had the inlined coding standards** — the expanded text in the transcript, not an `@docs/` reference.
- After the run, **no `sandcastle/*` branch or worktree remains for any merged item, and any unmerged item's branch still exists.** `git branch -d` refusing unmerged work is the whole safety argument.
- **Per-item wall-clock durations**, which are the only source for `repo.itemTimeout`'s default — currently an invented 45 minutes.
- **No branch was pushed and no pull request opened.**
- **A failed item's per-item log copied into `docs/manual-verification/`** — `.sandcastle/logs/` is gitignored, and a timed-out, crashed, zero-commit or transitively-skipped item leaves **no git trace at all**, so its log is the sole record of the outcomes that matter most.

Two things are **explicitly not covered** by any such run, and are named so they are not silently assumed proven — both inherited unproven from [#380](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/380), and neither a parallel behavior: the one-keystroke fast-path replay, and the Excess-deletion-commit-last ordering.

**On this repo's Swift suite under concurrency:** [#408](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/408) (an indefinite `XCTWaiter`/`CFRunLoop` deadlock from N=2 up) and [#409](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/409) (two tests asserting on unsettled state under load) both remain open and are **not this SPEC's to fix.** The per-item timeout makes the hang **bounded, not absent**. The tail's `.sandcastle/`-only rule below is what keeps a run off that trigger.

## Planned slice breakdown

Ordered so each slice is independently reviewable and **leaves the runner working** — the constraint that put pure moves ahead of the seam in [SPEC #371](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/371). Every slice runs `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test`.

Slices 1–10 build; slices 11–15 are the **tail**, and their shape is deliberate — see *The tail is a real wave* below.

1. **Move repo-shaped configuration into `.sandcastle/repo.mts`** — the pure move that de-Swifts the runner.
2. **Add the pure Work scope snapshot, ordering and level model** — `scope/snapshot.mts`, unwired, fully tested against hand-authored literals.
3. **Resolve Work scope against GitHub** — `scope/github.mts`, the fail-closed fetch layer plus the schema canary. Still unwired.
4. **Make the picker scope-first and teach the store to remember it** — the walk, the recovery paths, the run guard, `MAX_PARALLEL`, and the store's passthrough.
5. **Flip the contract to an allow-list and return a runner core from `prepare()`** — `DRIVERS`, the `sequential` and `whole-branch` drivers, `{{WORK}}`/`{{ANCHOR}}` injection, and the seam.
6. **Teach the draining drivers their outcomes, skips, tracker corrections and report** — the transitive skip set, the drift table, the settle-time reopen and comment, `code-review` on the anchor, the marker-prefixed report.
7. **Rewrite the three shipped prompts for `{{WORK}}` and `{{ANCHOR}}`** — lifted from `223868c`.
8. **Add the wave-parallel driver's worktrees, timeout, fan-in and cleanup** — plus the real-temp-git suite.
9. **Add the Planner and the Merger to the wave-parallel driver** — the hand-rolled validator, the semantic checks outside it, the fallback, the provable Merger skip.
10. **Register the wave-parallel workflow and render the run ledger** — the folder, the four prompts from `232f7d8`, and `itemLine` productionised from `PROTOTYPE-wave-run-report/`.
11. **Sweep the framework-agnostic and safety boundaries from registries** — tier 3, enumerating from `DRIVERS`, `WORKFLOWS` and the filesystem.
12. **Fix Review Only's stale `origin/main` baseline** — `Closes #417`.
13. **Dispose of the inert `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>` signal** — #410's finding 4, which #396 declined to inherit silently.
14. **Refresh `CONTEXT.md`'s Batch workflow glossary** — three stale entries, five ratified terms missing.
15. **Record the reopen rule and the testing admission rules in the ADRs** — and land `docs/worktree-parallelism-measurements.md` on a branch that reaches `main`.

### `ready-for-agent` is withheld from this SPEC until slice 5

**This issue deliberately does not carry `ready-for-agent` yet.** A **Specific SPEC** target must carry both `spec` and `ready-for-agent` — but that requirement only exists once [slice 5](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/422) lands the scope machinery that enforces it. Until then the label does nothing except make this SPEC a **pickable work item** for today's self-selecting loop, whose query is `gh issue list --state open --label ready-for-agent` with no dependency data — so an unattended run could pick this issue and try to implement all fifteen slices in one iteration.

**Add `ready-for-agent` back the moment slice 5 closes.** Nothing else re-adds it, and Specific SPEC will refuse this target without it.

### How this SPEC gets built

**This SPEC drains itself, in two harnesses.**

- **Slices 1–4** cannot be drained by a scoped run, because Specific SPEC does not exist until slice 4 lands and the seam until slice 5. Run them with whatever agent harness is at hand, or with today's Implement & Review, which still picks its own work.
- **Slices 5–10** are drainable by **Implement & Review under Specific SPEC** — one at a time, in the authored order, which is what the chain below expresses.
- **Slices 11–15** are drainable by **the wave-parallel workflow itself**, at `MAX_PARALLEL=3`. That is the point of the tail, and the reason for its shape.

### The tail is a real wave

Slices 1–10 are `blocked_by`-chained, so under any driver they are one work item per level — correct, and no test of concurrency at all. The tail is where the wave-parallel workflow gets exercised on real work, so it is shaped for that **by construction, authored now rather than retrofitted**:

- **Level 1: slices 11, 12, 13, 14** — mutually independent. A wave of three at `MAX_PARALLEL=3` leaves a remainder, which is what makes a second wave happen.
- **Level 2: slice 15**, `blocked_by` slice 11. The edge is substantive, not decoration: the admission rule *a sweep enumerates from a registry* is recorded against the sweeps that instantiate it, so the ADR cites shipped code rather than an intention.
- **All five are `blocked_by` slice 10**, so they are ineligible — an out-of-set blocker still excludes — until the wave-parallel workflow exists. When slice 10 closes, exactly these five become eligible and slice 11 is the only in-set blocker left, which is the precedence edge #394 introduced.

**Every tail slice touches only `.sandcastle/` or `docs/`, and that is load-bearing.** [#408](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/408)'s own trigger table is why a tail like this is runnable in *this* repo today: the deadlock needs **both** concurrency **and** a freshly-linked test bundle — at three to four concurrent runs with the bundle unchanged, **0 hangs in 15 items**. A slice that touched Swift sources would relink the bundle and re-arm it, and a wave of three would likely return three timed-out items 45 minutes apart. So the rule for anyone editing this tail: **a tail slice that touches `Sources/` or `Tests/` re-arms #408 and belongs in the build phase instead.**

**Do not retrofit an edge or reshuffle the tail to make a run look good.** If the shape stops holding, say so rather than adjusting the evidence.

### Explicitly not in this SPEC

- **Docker or container execution.** ADR-0001's rejection stands on an unchanged constraint: the macOS-only Swift package cannot build on Linux, so its mandatory verify loop would fail every iteration. Parallelism is host worktrees under `noSandbox()`.
- **Stacked pull requests, and any AFK publishing at all.** The run stays local; the handoff stays the Conductor branch review.
- **An unbounded Planner** that discovers its own work, as upstream's does.
- **Non-interactive CLI flags for bypassing the picker**, a new agent provider, letting Sandcastle execute `ready-for-human` or unreleased work, changing GitHub's sub-issue or dependency model, and widening a single implement→review loop beyond one work item.
- **The one-keystroke fast-path replay and the Excess-deletion-commit-last ordering**, inherited unproven from [#380](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/380). Named here so they are not silently assumed proven; neither is a parallel behavior.
- **Fixing [#408](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/408) or [#409](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/409).** Both are this repo's Swift suite under load, which this SPEC neither built nor can fix. The tail's `.sandcastle/`-only rule is how a real run stays off #408's trigger; proving the Swift suite tolerates concurrency is a separate effort and gates nothing here.
- **A `ready-for-human` slice of any kind.** Every issue in this tree is `ready-for-agent` so the SPEC can be drained AFK. Manual verification is one issue the maintainer files after the fact, against the checklist under *What only a real run can prove* — deliberately not a released slice, and deliberately not a gate an agent could tick.

repos/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418/.body:
Slice 1 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

## What

`runner.mts:31–33` hardcodes `swift package resolve`. The map's settled boundary is *"no toolchain-shaped constant may reach the runner"* and *"the runner never learns this is a Swift repo"* — already false today, and parallelism makes it worse: `createWorktree` executes only `host.onWorktreeReady`, so the worktree path needs a second hook site.

Add `.sandcastle/repo.mts`, the **only** per-repo module. Everything else in `.sandcastle/` becomes portable, so dropping Sandcastle into the web repo is one file to edit plus whatever prompts differ.

This is a pure move and it leaves the runner working.

## Shape

```ts
export interface RepoConfig {
  readonly onHostReady: readonly { readonly command: string }[];
  readonly onWorktreeReady: readonly { readonly command: string }[];
  readonly copyToWorktree: readonly string[];
  readonly maxParallelDefault: number;
  readonly itemTimeout: { readonly minutes: number };
}

export const repo: RepoConfig = {
  onHostReady:        [{ command: "swift package resolve" }],
  onWorktreeReady:    [{ command: "swift package resolve" }, { command: "swift build --build-tests" }],
  copyToWorktree:     [],
  maxParallelDefault: 3,
  itemTimeout:        { minutes: 45 },
};
```

Each value carries a reason, and the reason belongs in a comment beside it:

- **`copyToWorktree: []` is a finding, not a default.** Cloning `.build` *breaks the build* on an absolute PCH module-cache path, and removing that cache still recompiles all 446 files, while `pnpm install` cold is 0.6s.
- **`maxParallelDefault: 3`** because measured build throughput is 1.00, 1.48, 1.67, 1.60 at N=1..4 — it **inverts** at 4, since `swift build` already saturates 10 cores.
- **`itemTimeout` is provisional and must say so.** 45 minutes is invented; the maintainer's acceptance run calibrates it from real per-item wall-clock durations.
- **`onWorktreeReady` carries the pre-warm** that is this repo's substitute for the isolation ADR-0001 denies: running each bundle once alone removed every observed hang.

## Rules

- `runner.mts` reads `repo.onHostReady` and holds no command string of its own.
- **The runner may run a command whose output it discards. It may never run a command whose exit code it branches on — except git's, which is framework-neutral.**

Slice 2 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

**Blocked by #433.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

Add `scope/snapshot.mts`: the **pure** half of Work scope. Types, eligibility classification, canonical serialization and digest, the run order, the levels, and the transitive skip set. **No I/O, no `gh`, no network** — this module is what makes the map's biggest untested surface testable.

Nothing is wired to the picker or the runner in this slice. The runner keeps working untouched.

## Scope

```ts
export type WorkScope =
  | { kind: "specific-spec"; target: string }   // raw URL or number, unparsed
  | { kind: "specific-issue"; target: string }
  | { kind: "all-ready-for-agent" };
```

Kind literals are **kebab-case**, not the research doc's snake_case — nothing external consumes the snapshot, and two spellings for one concept is a defect.

`WorkScopeSnapshot` carries `schemaVersion`, `repository`, `scopeKind`, `anchorNodeId`, `memberNodeIds`, `executableNodeIds`, normalized `issues` with exclusion reasons, and `snapshotId`, a SHA-256 over canonical JSON. `IssueSnapshot` normalizes stable ids, repository/number/url, title/body, state, **lexically sorted** labels, **ascending-id** comments, native parent/child edges in authored order, and open blocker identities.

Pure functions this module owns:

- **Eligibility.** For Specific SPEC the anchor is controlling context but **not executable**; Specific issue allows only its anchor; `ready-for-human` **always overrides** `ready-for-agent`. Closed, unreleased, `ready-for-human` and out-of-set-blocked descendants stay visible with an exclusion reason and are excluded from the allow-list.
- **In-scope blockers are precedence edges, not exclusions.** A blocker that is itself in the eligible set *orders* its dependent; only a blocker **outside** the set still excludes. Without this a `blocked_by`-chained SPEC yields one eligible descendant per run and waves cannot exist.
- **A dependency cycle is detected and reported so the caller can abort before confirmation.**
- **Run order: a stable topological sort keyed on authored sub-issue order** — depth-first pre-order over each parent's `childNodeIds`, so a slice's own children precede the next sibling. The repository-wide queue has no parent, so it tie-breaks on **ascending issue number**.
- **Truncation is a prefix of that order, applied after the sort** — which is what guarantees the guard can never hand over an item whose blocker was cut.
- **Levels** are a pure function of `(list, accumulated skip set)`, recomputed at each wave boundary. Do not freeze them: a transitive skip shrinks what is ready.
- **The transitive skip set.** Given an item that produced no commits, crashed, timed out or was rewound, drop it and every in-set item `blocked_by` it, directly or through a chain. Independent items still run. **A skip never backfills** — item 11 is not promoted when item 3 is skipped.
- **Comment normalization drops any comment whose first line is `<!-- sandcastle-run-report -->`**, at every node and for every scope. This is a content filter over successfully fetched pages, not a tolerance for missing ones. Unmarked item-level bounce comments survive — they are real review context.
- **Flatten to work items:** Specific SPEC → every eligible descendant in run order; Specific issue → exactly one; All ready-for-agent → the eligible queue in run order.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scope/snapshot.mts` imports only `node:*` — no `child_process`, no fetch, no `gh`.
- [ ] Tests are **hand-authored topology literals**, not recorded fixtures: a literal states the edges where a reader can see them, and the cycle case and the blocker-outside-the-set case cannot be recorded without manufacturing them on the real tracker.
- [ ] Tests cover: recursive descendant discovery; eligibility filtering; single-issue isolation; the repository-wide queue's ascending order; the topological sort keyed on authored order; prefix truncation; **precedence edge vs exclusion**; cycle detection; level computation; levels shrinking under transitive skips; the marker filter keeping bounce comments; the canonical digest being stable across key order.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green, and the suite still spawns nothing.

## Decisions to honour

- [Establish the GitHub issue-tree snapshot and eligibility query](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/390) — the snapshot's fields, normalization and the eligibility rules.
- [Settle batch ordering, stop conditions, and handoff semantics](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/394) — precedence edges, the sort, truncation, the transitive skip, the marker filter.
- [Define the Work scope contract across runner and workflows](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/392) §1–§2 — the module split and the kebab-case literals.
- [Decide the Work scope test and acceptance strategy](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/396) — why literals and not fixtures.

Slice 3 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

**Blocked by #419.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

Add `scope/github.mts`: the **only** module that talks to GitHub. Parse a target, resolve it, traverse the tree, fetch comments and blockers, and build the frozen snapshot slice 2 defined. Plus the one recorded fixture that stands as a **schema canary**.

Still unwired — the picker reaches it in slice 4. The runner keeps working.

## The definitive read set

Pin `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` and `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10`. Paginate every list.

- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}` — canonical identity, body, state, labels
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/sub_issues?per_page=100`, **recursively** — native membership
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments?per_page=100` — acceptance and bounce context
- `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/dependencies/blocked_by?per_page=100` — blocker identities

## Rules

- **Parse the target locally.** A bare positive integer or an exact same-repository `/issues/<number>` URL. Build the API path from the fixed repository plus the parsed number, and reject a response that is a pull request or whose canonical repository/number differs. **`gh issue view --repo` is not a safe resolver for an untrusted URL** — a live probe showed the URL overriding `--repo` and resolving an `/issues/1` URL to a pull request.
- **Traverse the whole tree before filtering**, through closed, blocked, unreleased and `ready-for-human` intermediates. GitHub allows 100 children per parent, eight levels and cross-repository children, so missing pagination or dropping a foreign subtree would produce a false *drained* result.
- **`blocked` derives only from blockers whose current state is `open`** — `/blocked_by` returns closed relationships too.
- **Fail closed, always.** `404` surfaces as "not found or inaccessible" without pretending to distinguish them. A cross-repository or otherwise partial SPEC tree **aborts** scope loading; open foreign blockers stay visible gates but never become work. Any authentication, permission, rate-limit, service, pagination or comment-page failure **aborts before dispatch**. **An API failure is never an empty list.**
- **A pre-dispatch revalidation helper.** GitHub exposes no atomic recursive snapshot, so re-read the current item **and its ancestry** immediately before each dispatch and refuse on a mismatch. Ancestry lost `spec` or `ready-for-agent`, or closed → the caller aborts the run; the item itself changed → the caller skips by cause. Classifying the mismatch is this module's job; deciding what the run does is slice 6's.

## The schema canary

One recorded fixture, from a real `gh api` read of this SPEC's own tree, committed beside the tests and **skippable**.

Hand-authored literals share one fatal blind spot: `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` is a newer GitHub surface, and if GitHub renames or nests it, **every hand-authored test still passes while production sees zero blockers and dispatches a whole SPEC dependency-blind in the wrong order.** Tier 1 cannot catch it — our own type is the thing that would be wrong. One deliberately-refreshed fixture is the only thing that fails when reality moves.

Refreshing it needs the network and is **done deliberately, never automated**. Say so in the test file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scope/github.mts` is the only module in `.sandcastle/` that names a GitHub URL or endpoint path.
- [ ] Target parsing rejects: a negative or zero number, a foreign-repository URL, a pull-request URL, and a number that resolves to a pull request.
- [ ] Every abort path is tested, and none of them can return an empty snapshot.
- [ ] The canary fixture is committed, the test that reads it is skippable, and the file records how and when to refresh it.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

## Decisions to honour

- [Establish the GitHub issue-tree snapshot and eligibility query](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/390) — every rule above, and `docs/research/github-work-scope-snapshot-and-eligibility.md`.
- [Settle batch ordering, stop conditions, and handoff semantics](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/394) §6 — what a mismatch means.
- [Decide the Work scope test and acceptance strategy](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/396) — the canary and why it exists.

repos/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418/.body:
Slice 4 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

**Blocked by #420.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

Make Work scope the picker's **first** question, and teach the store to remember it. `cli/flow.mts` stays pure, synchronous and spawn-free, so the exact sequence of screens stays an assertion rather than a manual walk.

## The walk

Work scope → target → **resolve** → fast path → workflow → run guard → `MAX_PARALLEL` → models/effort → confirm.

1. **Work scope**, in this order: **Specific SPEC**, **Specific issue**, **All ready-for-agent issues**.
2. **Target** for an explicit scope: a bare number or a same-repository issue URL. Resolve over the network, then show number, title and labels.
3. **Reject in place.** Closed, blocked or unreleased targets are refused; every explicit target requires `ready-for-agent`, and Specific SPEC additionally requires `spec`.
4. **State eligibility.** Specific SPEC shows eligible versus excluded descendant counts; Specific issue states that exactly one issue will run; the repository-wide scope shows the queue count.
5. **Cancellation is safe at every prompt.** A validation failure or an empty scope keeps the resolved context and offers only the relevant recovery: retry GitHub, enter another target, choose another Work scope, cancel.

## The seam

Resolution is network I/O, so it is **injected into the driver**, following the `EffortsFor` precedent:

```ts
export type ResolveScope = (scope: WorkScope) => Promise<ScopeOutcome>;
```

The flow gains a third step kind so the *point at which* resolution happens stays inside the pure module. `Question` becomes `Step` and `nextQuestion` becomes `nextStep` — a union with a non-question member should not be called `Question`:

```ts
export interface ResolveStep extends StepBase {
  kind: "resolve";
  scope: WorkScope["kind"];
  needsTarget: boolean;
  initialValue?: string;   // pre-fills from the store, and again on recovery
}
export type Step = SelectQuestion | NumberQuestion | ResolveStep;
```

`Answer` widens to carry the resolution outcome; a failed outcome is what makes the flow return the recovery select. `cli/prompts.mts` performs the resolution, because it already owns I/O.

## The two numbers

- **The run guard is universal.** Asked whenever the driver drains **and more than one** work item is eligible. Range 1–50, default 10. Specific issue never asks. The runner truncates to it, and the confirmation reads `up to 10 of 30 eligible`, so a partially drained SPEC is stated rather than implied. It is a **brake on an unattended run's token budget**, not a work-selection choice — which is why it is universal across scopes.
- **`MAX_PARALLEL`** is asked only when the driver runs items concurrently, defaulted from `repo.maxParallelDefault`. A picker question rather than a constant because contention depends on what the Mac is doing *right now*.

`ResolvedPlan` gains `scope: WorkScopeSnapshot`, `maxWorkItems: number` and `maxParallel: number`. **The confirmation's Work scope and Eligible rows belong to `cli/flow.mts`, not to `runShape`** — that is what keeps `runShape` down to a single number and the anchor out of the workflow.

## The store

- **Answers only, never outcomes.** Stored: `lastWorkflowId`, `lastScope: { kind, target, origin }`, `maxWorkItems`, `maxParallel`, `agents`. Never stored: the snapshot, `snapshotId`, any wave plan, completed/bounced/skipped records, the run report, the anchor's title. This is what keeps GitHub the single source of truth about what is done.
- **Scope is pre-fill, not replay**, and the fast path moves to **after** resolution. Three properties follow, and they are the reason for the reordering: the fast path's hint can state eligibility, accepting it always starts a run, and **staleness needs no representation** — a stale, deregulated or drained target fails in place and lands in the recovery paths that already exist.
- **`origin` gates the target only.** `git rev-parse --git-dir`, a free sibling of the `--git-common-dir` call `runStorePath` already makes, and unique where a branch name is not. `kind` always pre-fills — it is a habit, visible as a labelled row, and a wrong default costs one arrow key. `target` is the work, and a wrong one is a number you might not read.
- **Version stays 2, and the top level gains passthrough.** `parseStoredRun` today builds from `agents`/`knobs`/`lastWorkflowId` only, so unrecognised top-level keys are dropped on parse and gone on the next write. Carrying them through absorbs the orphaned `knobs` key **with no special case**, and extends key-level upsert from ids to fields. **A version bump is the worst option here**: an old parser fails `version !== 2`, treats the store as empty, and destroys the agent picks as well.
- **`knobs.maxIterations` is not migrated into `maxWorkItems`.** Different parameters that happen to both be integers; migrating on that strength would run a number nobody chose.
- **`storeIsReplayable` gains two clauses:** a remembered **draining** workflow additionally requires `maxWorkItems`; a remembered **concurrent** one additionally requires `maxParallel`. The fast path vanishes for exactly one run after upgrade, and that walk's write fills the key in permanently.

## Keeping the runner working

`Knob`'s retirement lands with the seam in slice 5, but the run guard replaces `maxIterations` here, so **delete `sequential-reviewer`'s `maxIterations` knob declaration in this slice and bound its loop with the guard** — carried on `ResolvedPlan` and passed through `WorkflowContext` as an interim `maxWorkItems` field that slice 5 removes. Two number questions for one parameter must never both be on screen.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cli/flow.mts` imports no `@clack/prompts`, spawns nothing, and touches no `process.stdout`.
- [ ] Ordered-step-id tests pin the whole walk, including that the scope step is first and the fast path comes after resolution.
- [ ] Every recovery path is tested from a failed `ScopeOutcome`.
- [ ] Store tests cover: version-2 round trip, **a v2 fixture holding `knobs` round-tripping with `knobs` intact**, key-level upsert of a top-level field, the origin gate pre-filling `kind` but not `target` from a foreign worktree, and both new `storeIsReplayable` clauses.
- [ ] A run of Implement & Review still works end to end, bounded by the run guard.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

## Decisions to honour

- [Prototype the universal scope-first picker flow](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/391), as amended on the run guard.
- [Define the Work scope contract across runner and workflows](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/392) §5–§6.
- [Decide what the run store remembers about Work scope](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/393) — all seven decisions, plus its `maxParallel` follow-up comment.
- [Decide how the Planner proposes waves and how the runner bounds it](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/403) §5 — `MAX_PARALLEL` as a picker question.
- `.sandcastle/PROTOTYPE-scope-first-picker/` on `main` — the approved walk, runnable.
