repos/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418/.body:
Slice 5 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

**Blocked by #421.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

The seam. `contract.mts` stops describing a *list* and starts describing a *driver*, `prepare()` returns a runner core instead of a bare `Dispatch`, and two of the three drivers land.

This slice also **closes a live hole in shipped code** (see below) and **retires `Knob`**.

## The contract

```ts
export interface DispatchResult {
  readonly commits: readonly { readonly sha: string }[];
  readonly baseSha: string;
}

export interface DispatchOptions {
  readonly promptFile: string;
  readonly promptArgs?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
}
```

Decided by arithmetic, not taste: **across both shipped workflows the entire use of `RunResult` is `commits.length` and `baseSha`, and the entire use of `RunOptions` is `promptFile` and `promptArgs`.** It is also the only shape both `run()` and `Worktree.run()` can satisfy — `WorktreeRunOptions` is a separate, narrower interface with no `output`, `cwd`, `branchStrategy`, `copyToWorktree` or `timeouts`.

**The hole this closes.** ADR-0010 claimed `DispatchOptions`'s omissions mean no workflow can contradict ADR-0001. `Dispatch` returns Sandcastle's `RunResult`, whose `resume?`/`fork?` options type omits neither `branchStrategy`, `cwd` nor `hooks`, so this compiles today:

```ts
const implement = await dispatch(IMPLEMENTER, { promptFile: "implement-prompt.md" });
await implement.resume?.("keep going", { branchStrategy: { type: "merge-to-head" }, hooks: {} });
```

The omission list was defeated by the return type. **Flipping to a two-key allow-list is what fixes it** — an allow-list cannot be defeated by a return type, and it cannot silently widen when Sandcastle adds an option. `contract.mts` exports **no Sandcastle type at all**, so a Sandcastle upgrade becomes a runner-side edit. `stdout` stops crossing the seam too: a workflow that can read agent stdout can branch on model output.

`WorkItem` **does not live in `contract.mts`**. `Workflow` loses `knobs` and gains `driver`; `runShape` becomes `(workItems: number) => string`. `WorkflowContext.knobs` and slice 4's interim `maxWorkItems` both go. **`Knob`, `knobQuestion`, `resolveKnob`, `knobsFor` and the store's per-workflow knob bucket are deleted** — `maxIterations` was the only instance and it moved out from under it, so what remains is speculative generality. It is a net deletion.

## The drivers

```ts
prepare(plan: ResolvedPlan): RunCore
DRIVERS[plan.workflow.driver](core, plan.workflow)
```

`drivers/registry.mts` exports **`DRIVERS`**, keyed by id — a real registry, because slice 11's sweeps must enumerate from one rather than from a literal list of today's cases.

**Two drivers here:** `sequential` (one item at a time in the host checkout) and `whole-branch` (no work items). `wave-parallel` arrives in slices 8–10.

**Both work-item drivers invoke a per-item body with a dispatch scoped to that item.** The item is passed to the body to *read* — number, title, url — and is **never** passed to `dispatch`, because the dispatch already *is* that item:

```ts
await core.runWaves(async (item, dispatch) => {
  const implement = await dispatch(IMPLEMENTER, { promptFile: "implement-prompt.md" });
  if (!implement.commits.length) return;
  await dispatch(REVIEWER, {
    promptFile: "review-prompt.md",
    promptArgs: { REVIEW_BASE: implement.baseSha },
  });
});
```

The guarantee strengthens rather than weakens: *"a dispatch that names no work item does not compile"* becomes *"a dispatch cannot name a work item at all; the driver decided which one before the body ran."* It also removes a race the required-key shape permitted — two concurrent bodies dispatching against the same item.

**No worktree handle ever crosses the seam.** Sandcastle's `Worktree` carries `.close()`, `.createSandbox()` and `.interactive()`.

**Capability is strictly non-increasing.** Extending Sandcastle means reusing a driver, never reaching further. Adding a workflow is a new folder and zero contract change; adding an execution shape is a new driver and zero change to existing workflows.

## The preflight

`prepare()` returns the runner core a driver needs — providers, the frozen ordered work list, repo config, git helpers — so **the driver cannot be invoked without a value only a passing preflight produces.**

| Preflight | Source |
| --- | --- |
| every distinct model's CLI version and login | shipped |
| `gh auth status` | [#407](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/407)'s surviving list |
| workspace tree is clean | [#404](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/404) — `git merge` refuses over uncommitted changes |
| no leftover `sandcastle/*` branch or worktree | [#404](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/404) |
| the frozen, ordered, truncated work list exists | [#392](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/392) + [#394](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/394) |

The Planner's and Merger's CLIs come free — they are in `workflow.agents`, so `distinctModels` already covers them. **Levels must not become eager:** the *list* is frozen at `prepare`, the *levels* are a pure function of `(list, skip set)` recomputed at each wave boundary. Rejected: a worktree smoke test — eager validation earns its cost against failures that surface *late*, and a broken `git worktree` fails the first wave immediately.

## Prompt-arg injection

The runner writes the scope args on every dispatch; a workflow never does. One JSON arg per per-item dispatch, **`{{WORK}}`**, carrying the snapshot record verbatim with the ancestor SPEC as a nested `spec` key; **`{{ANCHOR}}`** for the whole-branch driver, always substituted, literal `null` under repository-wide scope. A body's `promptArgs` key that collides with a reserved name **throws and never overrides**. The runner must pass **JSON, not raw markdown**: an item body containing a fenced block would break straight out of a markdown splice.

Reserved names written by the runner or driver: `WORK`, `ANCHOR`, `READY`, `MAX_PARALLEL`, `WAVE`. The only key a body writes is `REVIEW_BASE`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `contract.mts` has no `import ... from "@ai-hero/sandcastle"` of any kind, type-only included.
- [ ] `Knob` and every helper around it are gone; the store no longer reads a knob bucket but still **carries** an existing `knobs` key untouched.
- [ ] `drivers/registry.mts` exports `DRIVERS`, and `sequential` and `whole-branch` are registered.
- [ ] `sequential-reviewer/workflow.mts` and `review-only/workflow.mts` are reduced to a driver declaration plus a body, and neither can name a work item.
- [ ] Every preflight in the table above is asserted, and `dispatch` provably does not exist before they pass.
- [ ] A body that sets `promptArgs: { WORK: "…" }` throws rather than overriding.
- [ ] Both shipped workflows still behave as they do today, end to end.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

## Decisions to honour

- [Re-shape the Work scope contract for Planner-driven parallel waves](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/405) §1–§4, §7–§8 — the whole slice, including the rejected alternatives.
- [Define the Work scope contract across runner and workflows](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/392) — what survives of it: runner-owned scope, no `scopeKind`, no forged work item, runner-written prompt args, the universal guard, `Knob`'s death.
- [Prototype scope-aware prompts](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/395) — one JSON `{{WORK}}`, and why JSON.
- ADR-0010, *`DispatchOptions` and `DispatchResult` are the contract's own types* and *A workflow declares a driver and supplies a body*.

Slice 6 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

**Blocked by #422.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

Teach the draining drivers what to do when things go wrong, and make the run tell the truth about itself. **Every stop condition turns on one question: does the foundation exist?**

`drivers/outcomes.mts` holds the pure logic. The side-effecting edge — three `gh` calls — sits in the drivers.

## Outcomes

**Two-phase, not one flat enum.** A loop outcome is known when the wave settles; a merge outcome exists only afterwards, and only for items that committed. One flat enum makes `{ outcome: "merged" }` representable for an item that timed out.

```
LoopOutcome  = committed | no-commits | crashed | timed-out
MergeOutcome = merged | conflict-rewound | skipped-upstream   // only for `committed`
```

**A bounce is an annotation on a committed item, never an outcome.** It merges like a success and its dependents proceed; it changes only the report. Listing it beside `crashed` would imply a structural consequence it explicitly does not have.

**The driver observes; the body returns `void`.** Every outcome comes from git, the process or GitHub — never from the workflow's testimony. A body that could return `committed` for an item that crashed would hand a workflow influence over the transitive skip set.

## Stop conditions

- **Zero commits** → drop the item **and every in-set item `blocked_by` it, transitively**. Independent items still run. `sequential-reviewer/workflow.mts:44`'s comment — *"the backlog is empty or everything left is blocked"* — is a conflation of two facts and dies with the whole-run `break`.
- **A bounce** → the code landed and was judged incomplete, so the run continues **including dependents**. Deliberately asymmetric with the above.
- **Reopen stays a real `gh issue reopen`**, because it is what makes the `code-review` condition correctly false. `review-prompt.md:41–43`'s claim that *"the reopened issue re-enters the implement queue"* is now false and is rewritten in slice 7.
- **Drift, by cause** (the revalidation from slice 3 classifies it):

| Mismatch | Foundation? | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Item closed mid-run | yes — someone did the work | skip the item, continue with dependents |
| Item deregulated (`ready-for-agent` removed, `ready-for-human` added, newly blocked from outside the set) | no | skip the item, **skip dependents transitively** |
| **Anchor** changed (closed, or lost `spec`/`ready-for-agent`) | n/a — the controlling contract is gone | **abort the run** before dispatch |

- **Membership is never refreshed. No skip is ever silent** — a run that quietly drops items is a run that lies about what it did.

## The tracker corrections

The predicate is **closed, yet nothing of this item reached the workspace branch** — a *predicate, never an outcome*, because the driver cannot see whether the implementer reached its close step and the contract forbids asking the workflow. Two acts on **different keys**:

- **Reopen** iff `closed ∧ unmerged`.
- **Comment** iff `commits exist ∧ unmerged`, whatever the issue's state.

The split is forced by the **bounced-and-rewound** item: already open, so no reopen fires, and its branch would otherwise be named in no durable place at all. Key the comment on recoverable commits, which the driver already has from `git rev-list --count`.

- **Per item at settle, not in an end-of-run sweep.** A broken merged tree aborts the run, nothing is auto-cleaned on abort and there is no resume — so a sweep never executes in precisely the run that went worst. Per-item correction is abort-safe by construction.
- **Over dispatched items only**, so the run never reopens an issue a human closed mid-run — the drift table answers that case differently and correctly.
- **A merged-but-bounced item gets neither act.** Open claims *unfinished*, which is exactly the reviewer's ruling; it never claimed no code exists.
- **In every draining driver.** `sequential`'s reading of *unmerged* is *zero commits*, which catches an `implement-prompt.md:68` violation neither driver could previously detect. `whole-branch` is untouched.
- **The comment is human-facing and carries the run-report marker**, so normalization drops it and no later agent reads it. `prepare()` guarantees a human cleared that branch before any later agent could act, so the branch it names is **stale by construction** — handing a worktree-sealed implementer a dangling reference and a reason to reach outside would be worse than saying nothing.
- **A reopen is a tracker correction, never work selection.** Written as a rule, not left to the skip set: a reopened item is **not eligible again in the run that reopened it**.

Comment shape, `closed ∧ unmerged`:

```
<!-- sandcastle-run-report -->
Reopened by Sandcastle — this item's work never reached `<workspace-branch>`.

Outcome:  conflict rewound
Branch:   sandcastle/374-extract-the-pane-store  (3 commits, unmerged)
Log:      <per-item log path>

The branch and its worktree are kept, and no force flag is used anywhere, so
nothing here can be destroyed by the run. `prepare()` will refuse the next run
until they are merged, salvaged or removed.
```

`commits ∧ unmerged` on an already-open item is identical but for the first line, which drops the reopen claim.

## Handoff

- **`code-review` on the anchor**, evaluated against **live GitHub state** at end of run: the anchor is **open**, carries `spec`, and **every `ready-for-agent` descendant is closed**. This makes `docs/agents/triage-labels.md:24`'s promise true rather than correcting it. A truncated list leaves descendants open and a bounce reopened its issue — both simply fail the condition, so **no special case is written for either**.
- **The runner never closes a SPEC.** That judgment has twice been a deliberate human call on this tracker, and a wrongly-closed SPEC is far harder to notice than a wrongly-labelled open one.
- **An aborted run posts its report and labels nothing.**
- **The report** replaces `main.mts:31`'s bare `All done.`, goes to stdout on every run, and additionally as **one comment on the anchor** opening with `<!-- sandcastle-run-report -->`:

```
<!-- sandcastle-run-report -->
Run summary — SPEC #371, 10 of 30 eligible
  completed  6
  bounced    1  #375 — criterion 4 unmet
  skipped    2  #376 no commits; #377 depends on #376
  drift      1  #378 → ready-for-human mid-run
  excluded   20 truncated by run guard
```

**The repository-wide scope gets no durable report** — there is no anchor to comment on. Accepted rather than given an invented home.

**Payoff, self-enforcing with no coordination:** every reopen lands before the `code-review` condition is evaluated against live state, so a drained SPEC with a rewound slice **correctly goes unlabelled**. Neither rule knows about the other.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `drivers/outcomes.mts` is pure and its whole truth table is unit-tested with no network and no git: the transitive skip, the drift table, the closed-but-unmerged predicate in all seven rows, and the two acts on their different keys.
- [ ] A merged-but-bounced item provably receives neither a reopen nor a comment.
- [ ] A transitively-skipped item is never touched on the tracker.
- [ ] Every comment body the run composes begins with the marker, and the reopen path passes no issue-close call — both statically assertable, and slice 11 asserts them.
- [ ] `code-review` is applied only when all three conditions hold, and never to a closed anchor.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

## Decisions to honour

- [Settle batch ordering, stop conditions, and handoff semantics](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/394) §3–§8.
- [Decide what the run does when an item's issue is closed but its work never merged](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/412) — all eleven sections.
- [Re-shape the Work scope contract](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/405) §5 — the two-phase outcomes and why they stay out of the contract.
- [Decide the AFK push and pull-request gate](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/407) — only what survives: the bounce discriminator, the dirty-worktree rule, no auto-clean on abort, no resume.

Slice 7 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

**Blocked by #423.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

Rewrite the three shipped prompts so the runner's Work scope reaches the agents, and no prompt discovers its own work. **The prose already exists** — lift it from commit `223868c` (branch `prototype/scope-aware-prompts-395`), which edited these exact files in place and passed all six include-hygiene checks with 120/120 tests green.

Verify reachability first: `git cat-file -t 223868c`. If it is unreachable from this clone, **report that and stop — do not reinvent the prose.**

## The guarantee, stated correctly

*Prove that neither prompt can query beyond the resolved Work scope* is **not structurally achievable**: the implementer must run `gh issue close`, so `gh` is in its hands and there is no tool allowlist to reach for. The achievable guarantee is the one the current prompt violates: **the prompt never tells the agent that other work exists.** `implement-prompt.md:5` hands it a hundred-issue listing and `:29–38` hands it a heuristic for choosing among them — the prompt actively teaches the behaviour being removed.

## `sequential-reviewer/implement-prompt.md`

- **Delete the `gh issue list` block** and replace it with one JSON promptArg, **`{{WORK}}`** — the snapshot record verbatim, with the ancestor SPEC as a nested `spec` key. **Zero shell blocks in the work section**, so there is no query in the prompt to widen. Measured token win: #376 put the expanded prompt at ~21k tokens, *most of it* that block.
- **Delete the Priority order section** (`:29–38`) and `:75`'s *"leave a comment on the issue and move on"* — an agent handed one item has nowhere to move on to, and the four categories were never labels.
- **`ready-for-agent` is no longer named in this prompt at all**; the label was only ever in the deleted query, and eligibility is entirely the runner's now.
- **The blocked path forbids a token commit and stays silent on the cascade:** *comment saying exactly what blocks you, then finish — close nothing, commit nothing; never make a commit to signal progress, an empty or token commit is worse than none because it reports work that did not happen.* An agent told that no commit drops a whole dependency subtree has a clear motive to manufacture one, which would corrupt the stop condition silently and unfalsifiably.
- `# Done` fires on the one item being committed, or blocked-and-commented.

## `sequential-reviewer/review-prompt.md`

- Takes the **same `{{WORK}}` record** and **no longer runs `gh issue view` at all** — re-fetching would hand the reviewer the implementer's own *Completed by Sandcastle* comment, a summary by the author arguing its work is correct.
- **The `Closes #<n>` line survives as a cross-check**: compare it against the record's `number`; a mismatch or a missing line is **a reportable Spec finding**, then review against the work item regardless — the work item is the contract, the commit message is a claim about it. This makes a wrong changelog anchor detectable for the first time.
- Rewrite `:41–43`'s claim that a reopened issue *"re-enters the implement queue"* — with a frozen list nothing re-enters. **Keep Reopen as a terminal state and a real `gh issue reopen`.**

## `review-only/review-prompt.md`

- **`{{ANCHOR}}`** arrives as a JSON issue record, **always substituted** — literal `null` under repository-wide scope, never an absent key.
- **The prompt branches on the `spec` label in the record it was handed**, so no `scopeKind` reaches the workflow. A trap sits in the obvious reading: under a SPEC anchor nobody has ever walked the SPEC's own criteria; under an issue anchor they were walked already against a tighter diff. Same prompt, opposite verdicts.
- **Axis 1 gains a third question, asked only when the anchor carries `spec`:** does the branch deliver the SPEC? Walk its own acceptance criteria, met or unmet. The criteria that live at SPEC altitude are the ones about how the pieces fit, and they are checked here or nowhere.
- **`:64`'s prohibition is kept and widened**, not weakened: never walk a *work item's* criteria — not a non-`spec` anchor's, and not those of any slice a `Closes` line names under a SPEC anchor.
- Questions 1 and 2 gain the anchor as a yardstick: a change no commit accounts for *and* the anchor does not ask for is the strongest form of the unaccounted-code finding.
- `null` routes into the existing degradation section, renamed **When there is no anchor**, which also skips question 3. **The diff range stays `origin/main...HEAD` in every scope** — the range is a property of the branch, not of the anchor.
- **Delete `review-only/workflow.mts`'s comment** rejecting an anchor knob as *"work selection wearing a different hat"*. It is void: the runner selects now.

## Two shipped tests become wrong

`sequential-reviewer.test.mts`'s *"sends the implementer no promptArgs"* and `review-only.test.mts`'s *"sends no promptArgs key at all, not an empty object"* both currently pass and both pin the absence this slice removes. Update them; do not delete the coverage.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No `gh issue list`, no Priority order section and no `ready-for-agent` string in any implement prompt.
- [ ] The reviewer runs no `gh issue view`.
- [ ] Review Only asks its third Spec question only when `{{ANCHOR}}` carries `spec`, and asks nothing about a work item's criteria under any anchor.
- [ ] `{{ANCHOR}}` is substituted on every path, including as literal `null`.
- [ ] All six checks in `__tests__/workflows/prompt-includes.test.mts` pass over the rewritten prompts.
- [ ] The two tests that pinned promptArgs absence now pin the new behaviour.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

## Decisions to honour

- [Prototype scope-aware prompts for Implement & Review and Review Only](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/395) — every decision, and the snapshot at `223868c`.
- [Settle batch ordering, stop conditions, and handoff semantics](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/394) §2, §5.
- [Prototype the parallel workflow's prompts](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/410) — corrections 1 and 2: a forgotten key **fails loudly** on the AFK path, and prompt args cannot inject a shell block.

repos/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418/.body:
Slice 8 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

**Blocked by #424.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

The wave-parallel driver's git and process mechanics: per-item host worktrees, the wall-clock timeout, `--no-ff` fan-in, conflict rewind, and merge-gated cleanup. **No Planner and no Merger yet** (slice 9), and the workflow is **not registered yet** (slice 10) — so this driver is unwired and the runner keeps working.

## Worktrees

- Every item in a wave runs in its **own host worktree**, cut from the workspace branch's **current tip**. Branch name: **`sandcastle/<issue-number>-<slug>`**, slug from the snapshot title, lowercased, non-alphanumerics collapsed, truncated. The runner composes it — the Planner carries numbers only.
- `createWorktree({ branchStrategy: { type: "branch" }, hooks })` plus `Worktree.run({ sandbox: noSandbox() })`. **`WorktreeRunOptions.sandbox` is required and does not default** — the defaulting belongs to `Worktree.interactive()`, which this runner never calls. Pass it explicitly.
- `CreateWorktreeOptions.branchStrategy` excludes `head` at the type level, so the alternative is a compile error rather than a convention.
- `createWorktree` accepts `hooks` but **executes only `host.onWorktreeReady`**; the rest pass through to the later `run()`. That is the seam `repo.onWorktreeReady`'s pre-warm needs, and it fires at worktree-creation time.
- **Host worktrees only, no container.** ADR-0001's rejection stands on unchanged reasoning; parallelism does not reopen it.

## The per-item timeout

- Built from `run()`'s `signal?: AbortSignal`. **Sandcastle's `Timeouts` covers lifecycle steps only** — copy, git setup, commit collection, merge-to-host — not the agent run.
- **`timed out` is an outcome distinct from `tests failed`.** A hang is not evidence about the work item, and the stop conditions all turn on *does the foundation exist* — a timeout answers neither yes nor no.
- Without one, a hung item stalls its wave until `idleTimeoutSeconds` (default 600) kills the silent agent, and orphaned test processes may outlive it. This is measured, not hypothetical ([#408](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/408)).
- Value from `repo.itemTimeout`. `signal` must **not** be reachable from `DispatchOptions`, or a workflow could defeat it.

## Fan-in

- When the wave settles, the runner merges each settled branch back into the workspace branch **`--no-ff`, in run order, not completion order**. Without `--no-ff` the first merge of each wave fast-forwards and that item's attribution disappears; with it, every item leaves a `Merge branch 'sandcastle/375-…'` commit — **the only per-item boundary in an otherwise flat diff.**
- The next wave's worktrees are cut from the **updated tip**, which is what the precedence-edge rule requires. **A partial wave still advances**; a wave where nothing settled leaves the tip untouched and needs no special case.
- **Fan-in is the runner's; verification is the prompt's.** The runner keeps only what git gives it free: merging, conflict detection from the exit code, the rewind to the pre-merge SHA, cleanup, and the timeout. No toolchain command may reach it.
- A conflict the run cannot resolve **rewinds that one item to the pre-merge SHA** and skips its dependents transitively; the item's branch still holds every commit and the merge is reproducible by hand. A merged tree that fails to build **aborts the run** — the asymmetry is attribution.
- **The reviewer still diffs `REVIEW_BASE...HEAD` inside its own worktree, before fan-in**, so it sees exactly its own item's commits on the wave base.

## Cleanup

- **A merged item's worktree and branch are deleted** with `git worktree remove` and `git branch -d`. Its commits are provably in the workspace branch, so the worktree is a copy, not work — ten items across three runs is otherwise thirty Swift worktrees carrying `.build`.
- **An item that crashed, timed out, produced no commits, conflicted or bounced keeps both.** `#407`'s *"no worktree is ever removed"* narrows to **"no unmerged worktree is ever removed"** — the property it was actually protecting.
- **No `--force`, `-D` or `-f` appears anywhere in the cleanup path.** Both steps are self-enforcing: `git branch -d` refuses an unmerged branch and `git worktree remove` without `--force` refuses a worktree with modified or untracked files. A refusal becomes **a line in the report, not an error.**
- **Nothing is ever auto-cleaned on abort, and there is no resume.** A dirty worktree is reported and never vetoes.
- `prepare()`'s leftover check (slice 5) is what refuses the next run.

## The test suite: a real temp git repo with a fake body

**You only fake what is expensive.** Agents cost money, minutes and a provider login, so `fakeDispatch` is forced. Real git costs nothing — the same reasoning as *"every provider factory is a plain object literal, so building the real ones costs nothing."*

It is also the **only** way to assert the three claims this topology rests on that are really claims *about git*:

1. `--no-ff` leaves exactly one merge commit per item as the sole per-item boundary;
2. a conflicting merge fails detectably enough to rewind one item;
3. **`git branch -d` refuses to delete unmerged work** — the entire no-force-flag safety argument.

Against an injected `Git` port all three would be asserted against a fake written by the same person who wrote the assumption.

- **The driver takes its repo root as an explicit parameter** — honest rather than test-only, since it operates on "the workspace repo".
- **Concurrency needs no real timing:** a fake body returns promises resolved in a chosen order, so a partial wave is deterministic.
- **Accepted cost, stated plainly:** this suite spawns processes and touches the filesystem, breaking the current 120-test *spawns nothing* property. Bought for the only proof the safety argument holds.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `drivers/wave-parallel.mts` names no toolchain command and no force flag.
- [ ] Against a real temp repo: fan-in produces one `--no-ff` merge commit per merged item, in run order, each naming its branch.
- [ ] A **partial wave** — `allSettled` with one rejected sibling — merges the others, does not merge the rejected one, skips its in-set dependents transitively, and **does not abort the run**.
- [ ] A conflicting merge rewinds exactly one item to the pre-merge SHA and leaves its branch intact.
- [ ] `git branch -d` is shown to **refuse** an unmerged branch, and the refusal is reported rather than thrown.
- [ ] `timed out` is distinct from both zero commits and a failing suite, and a timed-out item is not merged.
- [ ] Each item's `REVIEW_BASE` is that item's own base.
- [ ] An abort leaves every worktree and branch in place.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

## Decisions to honour

- [Decide the branch and pull-request stack topology and the wave fan-in](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/404) — §2, §3, §6, §7 and both corrections.
- [Measure worktree contention for concurrent Swift builds](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/406) — the timeout, the distinct outcome, the pre-warm.
- [Re-shape the Work scope contract](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/405) — the Sandcastle 0.12.0 fact list.
- [Decide the Work scope test and acceptance strategy](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/396) — real git, fake body, repo root as a parameter.
- ADR-0001, *Concurrent runs get one host worktree per work item* and *Parallelism does not reopen containers*.

repos/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418/.body:
Slice 9 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

**Blocked by #425.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

Add the two driver-internal host dispatches: the **Planner**, which may narrow a wave, and the **Merger**, which verifies the merged tree. Both are dispatched by the **driver**, not the workflow, and neither is a `Dispatch` — which is precisely why they alone may use `output`.

The workflow is still unregistered; slice 10 wires it.

## The Planner is a level splitter

The runner already computes membership, order and the levels. Upstream's Planner exists to *infer* a dependency graph from prose; ours is handed real `blocked_by` edges, so that job is the one job it definitively cannot have. What is left is the judgment the edges do not encode: **two ready items that rewrite the same module are unsafe to run together.**

- It is handed the **current ready level** and may only **subset** it. It cannot discover work, add an item, widen a wave, cross a level, name a branch or reach past the resolved Work scope.
- **An omitted item is deferred to the next wave, never dropped.**
- **The Planner never sees dependency edges** — as a level splitter it needs only the ready level (edges already applied), `MAX_PARALLEL`, and each item's number, title and body. **It runs no queries.**
- **Wave size *is* concurrency — there is no semaphore.** A semaphore would silently undo its only power: two items it separated could still overlap while a wide plan drains. A too-wide plan is a validation failure, not something quietly degraded.

## Plan shape and validation

```
<plan>{ "wave": [12, 15, 21],
        "deferrals": [{ "number": 18, "reason": "rewrites runner.mts, as does #12" }] }</plan>
```

Identity is **numbers only** — the runner supplies titles from the snapshot and names branches deterministically. Everything the runner already knows is a forgery surface if echoed back. `deferrals` are advisory prose, validated for shape but **not** cross-checked against the deferred set: a level splitter whose deferrals are unexplained is unauditable.

**Validation splits in two, and Sandcastle owns half.**

- **Shape** — `Output.object({ tag: "plan", schema, maxRetries: 1 })`. It does tag extraction, fence-aware JSON parse and Standard Schema validation, and on failure resumes the agent's own session with a token-efficient error description. Upstream's hand-rolled `<plan>` regex plus `throw` is obsolete at 0.12.0.
- **Semantics** — the runner's, applied **after** the dispatch returns: an item outside the current ready set → invalid; more than `MAX_PARALLEL` → invalid; **zero items → invalid**; duplicates → invalid. **Omitting ready items is legal — that is the power.**

**Semantic validation must live outside the Standard Schema validator.** The runner composes that validator per wave, so it *could* close over the ready set and get semantic retries free from `maxRetries` — which is exactly why it must not. Keeping semantics outside is what makes *no semantic retry* true rather than aspirational.

**A zero-item plan is invalid, not "done."** Forced, not chosen: upstream's `if (issues.length === 0) break` is its stop condition, but our ready set is runner-computed and known non-empty, so an empty plan can only mean *defer everything* — a livelock.

**An invalid plan falls back to the runner's computed wave** — the first `MAX_PARALLEL` of the ready level in settled order — with **no retry and no abort**. Valid by construction, because it is the same baseline used to validate. The stakes are lower than they look: each item builds in its own worktree off a common base, so a bad co-schedule costs a rebase conflict at fan-in, not a corrupted run.

**The fallback renders a wave-level ledger line.** This is not optional and it is not decoration. Three decisions compose badly — the silent fallback, a prompt that never mentions it, and seven outcomes that are all per-*item* — so **the Planner's failure mode was designed to be invisible**: every wave could silently become the computed wave, the run completes, every item merges, the ledger looks perfect, and the destination's one genuinely new component has never once worked. **Telling the human after the run is not telling the agent during it**; `plan-prompt.md` stays silent, and the maintainer reads the ledger. Do not later tidy this line away for consistency with the prompt.

**One dispatch per wave, skipped when the ready level holds exactly one item** — a zero-item plan being invalid means the only valid plan is that item. **Not** skipped merely because the level fits `MAX_PARALLEL`: at `MAX_PARALLEL = 3` a two-item level can still hold two items that must not run together.

## The Merger

- **Dispatched once per settled wave**, on the host with no worktree, handed whatever happened — nothing, a conflicted branch, a broken tree, or both.
- **The runner still merges in code.** An agent never merges what git merges cleanly, and paying an agent to run three clean `git merge --no-edit` calls is waste that also makes the merge non-deterministic.
- **Skipped when exactly one branch merged cleanly into an unmoved base.** The merged tree is then identical to that branch's tree, which the item's own implement→review loop already gated — a git fact rather than a guess about the toolchain. On a narrow SPEC, or any wave the Planner splits to one, it is the common case.
- **It never closes an issue.** Upstream's CLOSE ISSUES section dies entirely: the runner never closes a SPEC and the implementer already closes its own item.
- **It reports through `<merge>` structured output** — `{ "verified": bool, "unresolved": [...], "notes": "…" }` via `Output.object({ maxRetries: 1 })`, the same idiom as the plan so the folder has one, not two. Forced, not preferred: the runner **cannot re-derive the verdict** (it may not run the toolchain command), and **a completion signal is not a capability the run has** — `runner.mts` sets no `completionSignal`, so `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>` is inert and would carry no payload anyway.
- `verified: false` with unresolved conflicts → those items rewind. `verified: false` on a tree that merged cleanly → **the run aborts.** Never conflate them.
- **Accepted cost:** a clean multi-item wave pays one dispatch that usually runs two commands and returns. That is the price of the runner not knowing what language the repo is written in.

## Two implementation facts

- **There is no zod.** `.sandcastle/package.json` has exactly two dependencies. Hand-roll the `StandardSchemaV1` validator — the interface is small and both schemas are two fields — rather than adding a dependency to a deliberately tiny package. One validator, two uses.
- **`maxRetries` requires provider session resume**, and `run()` **fails at entry** when retries are requested of a provider that cannot resume. `claude-code` and `codex` both resume, so `maxRetries: 1` is safe for every provider the registry offers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `PLANNER` and `MERGER` join `agents/catalog.mts`, so the picker resolves their models and `distinctModels` preflights their CLIs.
- [ ] The hand-rolled `StandardSchemaV1` validator is used by both `<plan>` and `<merge>`, and adds no dependency.
- [ ] Semantic plan validation is provably outside the schema validator, and each invalid case — wrong level, zero-item, over-width, unknown number, duplicate — **falls back with no retry and no abort**.
- [ ] The fallback renders a **wave-level** ledger line, asserted in a test.
- [ ] The Planner dispatch is skipped at a one-item level and **not** skipped at a two-item level under `MAX_PARALLEL = 3`.
- [ ] The single-item Merger skip is a pure function of a wave's merge outcomes and is unit-tested.
- [ ] The Merger's `verified: false` paths are distinguished: unresolved conflicts rewind; a cleanly-merged broken tree aborts.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

## Decisions to honour

- [Decide how the Planner proposes waves and how the runner bounds it](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/403) — all eight sections.
- [Decide the branch and pull-request stack topology and the wave fan-in](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/404) §4 and its correction.
- [Prototype the parallel workflow's prompts](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/410) decision 3 — why `<merge>` and not a completion signal.
- [Decide the Work scope test and acceptance strategy](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/396) — the Planner's invisible failure mode.
- ADR-0010, *The Planner does not weaken "a workflow holds control flow and nothing else"*.

Slice 10 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

**Blocked by #426.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

Register the third workflow and give the driver its display. After this slice the wave-parallel workflow is selectable, and the SPEC's own tail (slices 11–15) becomes drainable by it.

## The workflow folder

`.sandcastle/workflows/wave-parallel/` — `workflow.mts` plus four prompts. The `workflow.mts` declares `driver: "wave-parallel"`, its four agents, a `runShape` like `plan → implement → review, waves of up to 3, up to 10 issues`, and **one per-item body**, byte-for-byte what `sequential-reviewer` writes.

Add it to `WORKFLOWS`. **The sequential workflow stays** — it is the right choice when contention or a one-item scope makes concurrency pointless, and keeping it means nothing already shipped breaks.

## The four prompts

Lift verbatim from commit `232f7d8` (branch `prototype/parallel-prompts-410`). Verify first with `git cat-file -t 232f7d8`; if unreachable, **report it and stop rather than reinventing the prose.**

- **`implement-prompt.md` and `review-prompt.md` are byte-identical copies** of `sequential-reviewer`'s pair as slice 7 leaves them. Sandcastle already does everything a variant would have needed: `preprocessPrompt` expands shell blocks at `ctx.sandboxRepoDir`, which on the worktree path *is* the worktree; `Worktree.run()` injects `SOURCE_BRANCH`/`TARGET_BRANCH` as the item's branch and rejects any override; the agent's cwd is the worktree. **Beyond `{{WORK}}` a worktree dispatch needs no argument.** Copies keep ADR-0010's folder seam absolute at the cost of a fix applied twice, which is detectable as a plain file comparison — asserted in slice 11.
  - **A shared `prompts/` directory is rejected**: it gives up the property the folder seam bought, that a reader of the folder sees everything the agent was told. **Naming `../sequential-reviewer/implement-prompt.md` is rejected** and is not even expressible — `promptFile` is a bare filename resolved against `Workflow.dir`.
- **The implementer is never told its siblings exist.** No mention of concurrency, the wave or the fan-in. It is alone in its worktree and can observe nothing; `Implement only your work item` already forbids the edits that conflict; conflict cost belongs to the Merger. Rejected: a footprint warning that names no other work — still a hint that something else touches those files, and unfalsifiable prose no test can check.
- **`plan-prompt.md`** takes two args — `{{READY}}` (a JSON array of `number`, `title`, `body`) and `{{MAX_PARALLEL}}` (a scalar). Zero shell blocks, no included documents: the Planner needs neither the coding standards nor the tracker conventions, it sits on the critical path before every wave, and the one document that teaches `gh` has no business in the context of an agent that must run no commands. It states the cost asymmetry outright — *a wrong deferral costs a wave; an unflagged overlap costs one merge, so when the items do not tell you they collide, put them in the wave* — and **stays silent on the fallback**.
- **`merge-prompt.md`** takes one JSON `{{WAVE}}` (the branch, the pre-wave `base` SHA, `merged` with each merge commit, `unmerged` with conflicted paths), states its precondition (*the runner has already rewound each failed merge, so your working tree is clean and holds exactly the merged items*), carries this repo's verify loop and says why (*every item's own loop already ran this against its own branch; you are running it against the combination, which nothing else in the run ever sees*), includes the coding standards and **deliberately omits `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`**. Its section **The distinction that must not blur**: a conflict belongs to exactly one branch; a broken tree belongs to none — *never report a failing build as an unresolved conflict, and never abandon a branch because the tree does not build.* Repair scope is bounded by attribution: fix the integration, not the feature. Its rules: never touch the tracker, never push or open a pull request, never use a force flag, never reset/rebase/rewind/delete, implement nothing.
- **`MAX_PARALLEL` is passed as a string** — `promptArgs` is `Readonly<Record<string, string>>`, and `substitutePromptArgs` calls `.toString()` on every value anyway.

## The ledger

Productionise `drivers/ledger.mts` from `.sandcastle/PROTOTYPE-wave-run-report/render.mts` (already on `main` via [#413](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/pull/413)), then **delete both `PROTOTYPE-*` folders and their `package.json` scripts** — they are throwaway by construction and their decisions are now shipped code.

- **Append-only, never a repainting dashboard.** Three reasons, all recorded: the run is AFK and what the maintainer needs on return is a scrollback they can read top to bottom; a dashboard **cannot own the cursor it needs**, because `printFileDisplayStartup` writes two unsuppressable `console.log` lines per dispatch straight into the middle of a pinned block; and it degrades to nothing when piped, which is the obvious thing to do with an unattended run.
- **Concurrency forces `file` logging mode.** `LoggingOption` has **two** variants at 0.12.0, not three, and `stdout` resolves to `ClackDisplay` — spinners and `taskLog`, i.e. cursor control — so three concurrent dispatches would fight over one cursor. Per-item log files are the only permitted shape, and `buildLogFilename` already keys on branch and agent name, so the driver arranges nothing.
- **`onAgentStreamEvent` exists only on the `file` variant** and is the one live per-agent signal available — in exactly the mode concurrency forces.
- **Liveness is a sparse ten-minute metronome plus a five-minute silence alarm**, with a matching resume line — ~14 lines per 84-minute run. Rejected: a two-minute per-item metronome (~120 heartbeat lines against ~50 real ones **buries the record it lives in**) and the alarm alone (a healthy run then goes silent for fifteen minutes, so frozen and working look identical). The alarm flags a wedged item **thirty minutes before its timeout does**. **Elapsed renders against the item timeout**, because that is the only thing that will end a hang.
- **One `itemLine` serves the live view and the end-of-run report**, so a line learned at 02:00 reads the same in the morning and **nothing is report-only**. Seven outcomes across two phases; **`timed out` carries its own glyph and its own colour and shares neither with `crashed`**; `↩ bounced` and `↻ reopened` **compose** on one line rather than being one optional suffix.
- **Progress is `n/10 settled` against the frozen selection.** Membership is frozen and truncation is a prefix, so a transitive skip **settles** an item rather than shrinking the total — the fraction only grows, which is the property that makes it readable at a glance.
- **A failure interrupts no sibling, and the display never asks a question** — there is nobody there to answer it.
- **The log path is repeated only where it becomes useful**: one indented line under a silence alarm, and under `crashed`, `timed out`, `no commits` and `conflict rewound`. An approved item never gets one — there is nothing to read.
- Plus slice 9's **wave-level fallback line**.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `wave-parallel` is registered in `WORKFLOWS` and selectable, and both existing workflows are unchanged in behaviour.
- [ ] The four prompts match `232f7d8` byte for byte, except that `implement-prompt.md` and `review-prompt.md` match **slice 7's** sequential pair byte for byte.
- [ ] All six checks in `prompt-includes.test.mts` pass over the new folder **with no edit to the test** — it sweeps `WORKFLOWS` by `dir`, so the folder is covered on arrival by construction.
- [ ] `<plan>` and `<merge>` each appear literally in the prompt whose dispatch sets `output` — `run()` throws `output tag <x> not found in the resolved prompt` otherwise.
- [ ] `itemLine` is tested for all seven outcomes in **both** renderings, with both annotations composing, and `n/10 settled` shown to be monotonic under a transitive skip.
- [ ] Both `.sandcastle/PROTOTYPE-*/` folders and their scripts are deleted.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

## Decisions to honour

- [Prototype the parallel workflow's Planner, Merger and worktree prompts](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/410) — all five decisions and all five corrections.
- [Prototype how a wave-parallel run reports progress in one terminal](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/411) — the ledger, the heartbeat, the five library facts.
- [Decide what the run does when an item's issue is closed but its work never merged](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/412) §8 — composable annotations.
- ADR-0010, *A workflow declares a driver and supplies a body* and the amended **Layout**.

Slice 11 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418). **Tail slice — see the SPEC's *The tail is a real wave*.**

**Blocked by #427.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

Tier 3 of the test strategy: **static sweeps over source as data.** This is the only tier that covers code which does not exist yet, which is what the destination's *every current and future workflow* clause requires. No compiler and no behavior test can deliver that, because both only see what has been written.

## The admission rule, which is the load-bearing part

> **A sweep enumerates from a registry or the filesystem, never from a literal list of today's cases.**

Written as three hardcoded assertions about `runner.mts`, `sequential` and `wave-parallel`, *"no toolchain command reaches a driver"* silently stops covering the fourth driver added later — which is precisely how a framework-agnostic boundary rots while the suite stays green. Enumerate from `DRIVERS`, from `WORKFLOWS` (by `dir`), or from a `readdir`; never from an array of names.

## The sweeps

- **No toolchain command in `runner.mts` or in any module `DRIVERS` names.** The rule behind it: *the runner may run a command whose output it discards; it may never run a command whose exit code it branches on — except git's.* `swift package resolve` was hardcoded at `runner.mts:31–33` before slice 1.
- **No `--force`, `-D` or `-f` anywhere in any driver's cleanup path.** This is the whole safety argument: git itself refuses to destroy unmerged work, and a flag would take that away.
- **The worktree-variant prompts are byte-identical to the sequential pair** — a plain file comparison, enumerated from `WORKFLOWS`.
- **Reserved prompt-arg names do not collide.** `WORK`, `ANCHOR`, `READY`, `MAX_PARALLEL`, `WAVE` (runner- and driver-written) against `REVIEW_BASE` (the only key a body writes). At five names this is worth an assertion rather than a convention.
- **`contract.mts` exports no Sandcastle type**, and imports none even type-only.
- **The reopen path passes no issue-close call, and every comment body the run composes begins with `<!-- sandcastle-run-report -->`.**
- **No prompt contains a standalone shell block that mutates git state** (`git fetch`, `git pull`). `preprocessPrompt` expands every block with `{ concurrency: "unbounded" }`, so a block that another block depends on is a race — the defect [#417](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/417) records. Slice 12 fixes the instance; this rule stops the next one. The existing `prompt-includes` sweep cannot catch it, because it checks include *hygiene* and has no notion of one block depending on another block's **effect**.
- **`<plan>` and `<merge>` appear literally in the prompts whose dispatch sets `output`.**

## Rules

- **No silent caps.** If a sweep cannot cover something it names, it says so out loud rather than passing quietly.
- Sweeps live beside the existing `__tests__/workflows/prompt-includes.test.mts`, in its shape.
- This slice touches **only `.sandcastle/`**. A tail slice that touched `Sources/` or `Tests/` would relink the Swift test bundle and re-arm [#408](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/408), breaking the wide wave the tail exists to be.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every sweep above exists and enumerates from `DRIVERS`, `WORKFLOWS` or the filesystem — **`grep` the test files for a literal array of driver or workflow names and find none.**
- [ ] Each sweep is shown to fail against a deliberately-planted violation, then pass once it is removed. A sweep nobody has seen fail is a sweep nobody knows works.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

- [Re-shape the Work scope contract](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/405) §3, §6 — the two rules two of these sweeps enforce.
- [Decide the branch and pull-request stack topology](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/404) §6 — the no-force-flag rule.

repos/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418/.body:
Slice 12 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418). **Tail slice — see the SPEC's *The tail is a real wave*.**

**Blocked by #427.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

Closes #417.

## What

`review-only/review-prompt.md` fetches `origin/main` in one shell block and diffs against it in two others. **Sandcastle expands all shell blocks concurrently with unbounded concurrency**, so the diff and the log can run before the fetch completes — and the reviewer silently reviews against a stale `origin/main`.

Confirmed at the library level: `preprocessPrompt` (`@ai-hero/sandcastle@0.12.0`, `dist/index.js:65-125`) launches every `` !`…` `` block with `{ concurrency: "unbounded" }`. Document order determines only where the *output* is spliced back in — the loop that rebuilds the string runs after `Effect.all` settles — **so the ordering a reader infers from the file is not the ordering that executes.**

| Line | Block |
| --- | --- |
| 21 | `` !`git fetch origin main` `` |
| 31 | `` !`git diff origin/main...HEAD` `` |
| 37 | `` !`git log origin/main..HEAD` `` |

## Why it matters

The reviewer's entire input is the diff. A stale `origin/main` means the review is computed against the wrong base, and it fails **silently and plausibly**: the review completes, names its axes, and reaches a terminal state. Nothing reports that its diff was wrong. Severity scales with how stale the local ref is, which is why it survived a completed acceptance run undetected.

**It gets worse under waves** — the wave-parallel workflow runs up to three items concurrently, each expanding its own prompt, so one wave can produce three independently wrong review baselines while the concurrent `git fetch` invocations contend on the same ref store.

## The fix

Collapse the dependency into a single block so ordering is the shell's rather than the scheduler's:

```
!`git fetch origin main && git diff origin/main...HEAD`
```

and likewise for the log — or fetch once in a block whose output is discarded and chain both reads after it. Keep the spliced output in the same place in the document so the prose around it still reads correctly.

**Slice 11 owns the general rule** (no standalone git-mutating shell block, enumerated over every prompt). This slice owns the instance. If slice 11 has already landed, its sweep should be failing on this file — check that it is, and that it passes afterwards.

Sweep every other prompt for the same shape while here: any two blocks where one depends on the other's *effect*.

## Rules

- This slice touches **only `.sandcastle/`**. A tail slice that touched `Sources/` or `Tests/` would relink the Swift test bundle and re-arm [#408](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/408), breaking the wide wave the tail exists to be.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No prompt in `.sandcastle/workflows/` contains a standalone `git fetch` or `git pull` block.
- [ ] Review Only's diff and log are each chained after their own fetch, in one block.
- [ ] All six existing `prompt-includes` checks still pass — in particular **no backtick inside a block** and **every block on its own line**.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

## Decisions to honour

- [#417](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/417) — the finding, the library confirmation and the suggested fix.
- [Decide the Work scope test and acceptance strategy](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/396) — *a bug living only in a closed issue's comment is exactly as lost as an unrun criterion*, which is why this was re-filed.

Slice 13 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418). **Tail slice — see the SPEC's *The tail is a real wave*.**

**Blocked by #427.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

Every shipped prompt ends with `<promise>COMPLETE</promise>`. **It is documentation, not a mechanism.** `runner.mts` sets no `completionSignal` at all, and `maxIterations: 1` ends the iteration regardless — so the tag has never done anything, in any prompt, on any path.

It has been inherited silently through four prompt rewrites, and slice 10 copies it into three more files. [#410](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/410) recorded it as finding 4 and asked for an explicit decision rather than another silent inheritance; [#396](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/396) did not take it. **Take it here.**

## The two honest options

Pick one, record why in the commit body, and make the choice enforceable.

1. **Delete the tag from every prompt.** Cheapest and most honest: an inert marker that looks load-bearing is worse than no marker, and every reader who has met it has had to work out that it does nothing. Add a sweep rule in slice 11's shape — no prompt contains a `<promise>` tag — so it cannot drift back.
2. **Make it real** by setting `completionSignal` on host dispatches and having the driver read it. Note the ceiling before choosing this: **`WorktreeRunOptions` has no `output`**, and the two-key allow-list denies a body both `output` and `completionSignal`, so a per-item prompt's verdict can never become machine-readable this way. Whatever it buys is available on host dispatches only — where the Planner and Merger already have `Output.object`, which carries a payload a signal does not.

The reasoning strongly favours option 1, and the one thing that must not happen is a third silent inheritance.

## Rules

- Whatever is chosen, the **reviewer's terminal state stays prose and GitHub state**. That is what the bounce discriminator already assumes: re-read the item from live GitHub when it settles, and open means bounced.
- This slice touches **only `.sandcastle/`**. A tail slice that touched `Sources/` or `Tests/` would relink the Swift test bundle and re-arm [#408](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/408), breaking the wide wave the tail exists to be.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The decision is recorded in the commit body, with the reason and the rejected option.
- [ ] Every prompt in `.sandcastle/workflows/` is consistent with it — no file left half-migrated.
- [ ] The choice is enforced by a sweep in slice 11's shape, enumerating from `WORKFLOWS` by `dir` so a new folder is covered on arrival.
- [ ] If the tag is kept anywhere, the prompt says plainly what reads it.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

## Decisions to honour

- [Prototype the parallel workflow's Planner, Merger and worktree prompts](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/410) — finding 4, and decision 3's ceiling on what a completion signal can carry.
- [Re-shape the Work scope contract](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/405) §3 — the two-key allow-list that denies a body both keys.

Slice 14 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418). **Tail slice — see the SPEC's *The tail is a real wave*.**

**Blocked by #427.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

`CONTEXT.md`'s **Batch workflow** section (from line ~217) is the repo's ubiquitous-language record, and it now describes a Sandcastle that no longer exists. Three entries are stale and five ratified terms are missing. [#397](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/397) found this while amending the ADRs and handed it here rather than guessing at the wording.

## Stale, and why

- **Batch** — *"the set of issues one run works through: either a SPEC's open, released slices (a scoped run) or the whole `ready-for-agent` queue."* The choice is now three, not two, it is called **Work scope**, and it is asked **first**, before Workflow. Membership is frozen, ordered and truncated by a run guard before any workflow exists.
- **The implement→review loop** — *"an agent picks one slice from the batch"* is now false in the one way this whole map exists to fix: **the runner selects; no agent chooses what to work on.** The loop is also no longer the workflow's — *there is exactly one loop over work items per run, and it belongs to the driver.*
- **Handoff** — *"a drained SPEC (every released slice closed) is labeled `code-review` and gets a per-slice summary."* Now true rather than aspirational, but with conditions the entry does not state: the anchor must be **open** and carry `spec`, the runner **never closes a SPEC**, an aborted run labels nothing, and the repository-wide scope has no anchor and so gets no durable report.

## Missing, and ratified

- **Work scope** — the run's universal first input; three kinds, resolved to a frozen snapshot and flattened to an ordered work list before any workflow sees it.
- **Driver** — the runner-side module that turns work items into dispatches (`sequential`, `wave-parallel`, `whole-branch`); owns worktrees, concurrency, fan-in, skips and cleanup. A workflow declares a driver and supplies its **body**, the per-item implement→review sequence. Capability is strictly non-increasing.
- **Level** and **wave** — a level is one topological level of the run order; a wave is the set actually dispatched concurrently. **A wave is a subset of a level and never spans two, and wave size *is* concurrency.**
- **Planner** and **Merger** — the agent that may only *subset* the current ready level, and the per-wave agent that verifies the merged tree and repairs a conflict or a breakage. **The Merger does not do the merging; that is the runner's.**
- **Fan-in** — the runner merging a settled wave's branches back into the workspace branch with `--no-ff` in run order.
- **Repo config** — `.sandcastle/repo.mts`, the single per-repo file; every other module in `.sandcastle/` is portable.

Also: **there is no stack and no layer**, and **`ready-for-agent`, never "AFK-ready label"**, in user-facing copy.

## Rules

- **`CONTEXT.md` is a vocabulary record, not a design document.** Give each term a definition, not its reasoning — the reasoning lives in the ADRs and the closed tickets, and duplicating it creates a second copy that drifts.
- Match the section's existing voice and entry shape exactly.
- Docs only. This slice touches no `Sources/` or `Tests/` — a tail slice that did would relink the Swift test bundle and re-arm [#408](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/408), breaking the wide wave the tail exists to be.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three stale entries are corrected, and none of them still says an agent picks its work.
- [ ] All eight missing terms above are present, each in one or two sentences.
- [ ] No entry restates a decision's reasoning; each links or defers to the ADR instead.
- [ ] `CONTEXT.md`'s opening summary still describes the document accurately.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green (unchanged, but the gate stays).

## Decisions to honour

- [Amend the Sandcastle ADRs for universal Work scope and parallel worktrees](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/397) — the finding, and the two amended ADRs as the source of the definitions.
- [map #389](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/389)'s **Canonical language** block — the ratified spellings, verbatim.

Slice 15 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418). **Tail slice — see the SPEC's *The tail is a real wave*.**

**Blocked by #427, #428.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

Blocked by slice 11, deliberately: the admission rule *a sweep enumerates from a registry* is recorded **against the sweeps that instantiate it**, so the ADR cites shipped code rather than an intention.

## What

Three documentation debts that outlive this SPEC, and one file that is on no branch reaching `main`.

## 1. The reopen rule — ADR-0010

[#397](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/397) closed while [#412](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/412) was still being grilled and deliberately left this hole rather than guessing it. #412 §11 supplies the text. Add it under **Work selection is the runner's, and it is universal**, beside *the runner never closes an anchor*:

> **The runner reopens an item it closed falsely.** When a dispatched item's issue is closed but nothing of its work reached the workspace branch, the driver reopens it with a marked comment naming the branch. The runner never closes an issue and never reopens one to schedule work — a reopen is a correction to the tracker, never an act of work selection, and a reopened item is not eligible again in the run that reopened it.

## 2. The testing admission rules — ADR-0010

[#396](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/396) split its output **by lifespan**: the tier matrix is consumed once by this SPEC and then the tests *are* the record, but three rules **constrain unwritten code forever**, so they belong in an ADR. All three:

- **A sweep enumerates from a registry or the filesystem, never from a literal list of today's cases.** This is the rule that forced `DRIVERS` into existence, and a rule with that reach is an ADR.
- **The driver takes its repo root as an explicit parameter** — honest rather than test-only, since a driver operates on "the workspace repo" and naming it beats reading `process.cwd()` implicitly.
- **Fake only what is expensive.** Agents cost money, minutes and a provider login; real git costs nothing. This is why `fakeDispatch` exists and why the driver suite uses a real temp repo — and against an injected `Git` port the no-force-flag safety argument would be asserted against a fake written by the same person who wrote the assumption.

**Not `docs/TESTING.md`.** Its 587 lines mention Sandcastle zero times; it is a FoldWise Voice document about XCTest and SwiftPM coverage, and putting Sandcastle's strategy there **welds a portable tool to this repo**, against the map's explicit intent. `.sandcastle/TESTING.md` would be righter in principle, but ADR-0001 and ADR-0010 already govern Sandcastle from `docs/adr/`, and a second location costs more in split-brain than it buys.

## 3. Land `docs/worktree-parallelism-measurements.md`

[#397](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/397) found it **on no branch that reaches `main` and with no PR**, which is why ADR-0001's amendment cites [#406](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/406) rather than a path that would dangle. It holds the N=1..4 throughput series, the deadlock trigger table and the `copyToWorktree` finding — the evidence behind `maxParallelDefault: 3`, the per-item timeout and the pre-warm, and behind [#408](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/408) and [#409](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/409).

It is on branch `t3code/wayfinder-scope-map-issue-406`. Bring the file onto the workspace branch, then **update ADR-0001's amendment to cite the path** now that it resolves. Verify reachability first with `git cat-file -t`; if the branch is gone, report that rather than reconstructing the numbers — measurements cannot be rewritten from memory.

Slice 1 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

## What

`runner.mts:31–33` hardcodes `swift package resolve`. The map's settled boundary is *"no toolchain-shaped constant may reach the runner"* and *"the runner never learns this is a Swift repo"* — already false today, and parallelism makes it worse: `createWorktree` executes only `host.onWorktreeReady`, so the worktree path needs a second hook site.

Add `.sandcastle/repo.mts`, the **only** per-repo module. Everything else in `.sandcastle/` becomes portable, so dropping Sandcastle into the web repo is one file to edit plus whatever prompts differ.

This is a pure move and it leaves the runner working.

## Shape

```ts
export interface RepoConfig {
  readonly onHostReady: readonly { readonly command: string }[];
  readonly onWorktreeReady: readonly { readonly command: string }[];
  readonly copyToWorktree: readonly string[];
  readonly maxParallelDefault: number;
  readonly itemTimeout: { readonly minutes: number };
}

export const repo: RepoConfig = {
  onHostReady:        [{ command: "swift package resolve" }],
  onWorktreeReady:    [{ command: "swift package resolve" }, { command: "swift build --build-tests" }],
  copyToWorktree:     [],
  maxParallelDefault: 3,
  itemTimeout:        { minutes: 45 },
};
```

Each value carries a reason, and the reason belongs in a comment beside it:

- **`copyToWorktree: []` is a finding, not a default.** Cloning `.build` *breaks the build* on an absolute PCH module-cache path, and removing that cache still recompiles all 446 files, while `pnpm install` cold is 0.6s.
- **`maxParallelDefault: 3`** because measured build throughput is 1.00, 1.48, 1.67, 1.60 at N=1..4 — it **inverts** at 4, since `swift build` already saturates 10 cores.
- **`itemTimeout` is provisional and must say so.** 45 minutes is invented; the maintainer's acceptance run calibrates it from real per-item wall-clock durations.
- **`onWorktreeReady` carries the pre-warm** that is this repo's substitute for the isolation ADR-0001 denies: running each bundle once alone removed every observed hang.

## Rules

- `runner.mts` reads `repo.onHostReady` and holds no command string of its own.
- **The runner may run a command whose output it discards. It may never run a command whose exit code it branches on — except git's, which is framework-neutral.**
- Nothing else changes; a run behaves exactly as it does today.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.sandcastle/repo.mts` exists, exports `RepoConfig` and `repo`, and imports nothing from `workflows/` or `drivers/`.
- [ ] `grep -in swift .sandcastle/runner.mts` returns nothing.
- [ ] A run of Implement & Review still resolves Swift dependencies before the first dispatch.
- [ ] Every provisional or measured value carries its reason in a comment.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green.

- [Measure worktree contention for concurrent Swift builds](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/406) — every number above.
- ADR-0010, *Repo-shaped configuration lives in `.sandcastle/repo.mts`*.

Slice 2 of [SPEC #418](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/418).

**Blocked by #433.** Do not start this slice until every blocker is closed — the native dependency edge is authoritative, and this line exists so a runner that cannot read dependency edges still sees the order.

## What

Add `scope/snapshot.mts`: the **pure** half of Work scope. Types, eligibility classification, canonical serialization and digest, the run order, the levels, and the transitive skip set. **No I/O, no `gh`, no network** — this module is what makes the map's biggest untested surface testable.

Nothing is wired to the picker or the runner in this slice. The runner keeps working untouched.

## Scope

```ts
export type WorkScope =
  | { kind: "specific-spec"; target: string }   // raw URL or number, unparsed
  | { kind: "specific-issue"; target: string }
  | { kind: "all-ready-for-agent" };
```

Kind literals are **kebab-case**, not the research doc's snake_case — nothing external consumes the snapshot, and two spellings for one concept is a defect.

`WorkScopeSnapshot` carries `schemaVersion`, `repository`, `scopeKind`, `anchorNodeId`, `memberNodeIds`, `executableNodeIds`, normalized `issues` with exclusion reasons, and `snapshotId`, a SHA-256 over canonical JSON. `IssueSnapshot` normalizes stable ids, repository/number/url, title/body, state, **lexically sorted** labels, **ascending-id** comments, native parent/child edges in authored order, and open blocker identities.

Pure functions this module owns:

- **Eligibility.** For Specific SPEC the anchor is controlling context but **not executable**; Specific issue allows only its anchor; `ready-for-human` **always overrides** `ready-for-agent`. Closed, unreleased, `ready-for-human` and out-of-set-blocked descendants stay visible with an exclusion reason and are excluded from the allow-list.
- **In-scope blockers are precedence edges, not exclusions.** A blocker that is itself in the eligible set *orders* its dependent; only a blocker **outside** the set still excludes. Without this a `blocked_by`-chained SPEC yields one eligible descendant per run and waves cannot exist.
- **A dependency cycle is detected and reported so the caller can abort before confirmation.**
- **Run order: a stable topological sort keyed on authored sub-issue order** — depth-first pre-order over each parent's `childNodeIds`, so a slice's own children precede the next sibling. The repository-wide queue has no parent, so it tie-breaks on **ascending issue number**.
- **Truncation is a prefix of that order, applied after the sort** — which is what guarantees the guard can never hand over an item whose blocker was cut.
- **Levels** are a pure function of `(list, accumulated skip set)`, recomputed at each wave boundary. Do not freeze them: a transitive skip shrinks what is ready.
- **The transitive skip set.** Given an item that produced no commits, crashed, timed out or was rewound, drop it and every in-set item `blocked_by` it, directly or through a chain. Independent items still run. **A skip never backfills** — item 11 is not promoted when item 3 is skipped.
- **Comment normalization drops any comment whose first line is `<!-- sandcastle-run-report -->`**, at every node and for every scope. This is a content filter over successfully fetched pages, not a tolerance for missing ones. Unmarked item-level bounce comments survive — they are real review context.
- **Flatten to work items:** Specific SPEC → every eligible descendant in run order; Specific issue → exactly one; All ready-for-agent → the eligible queue in run order.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scope/snapshot.mts` imports only `node:*` — no `child_process`, no fetch, no `gh`.
- [ ] Tests are **hand-authored topology literals**, not recorded fixtures: a literal states the edges where a reader can see them, and the cycle case and the blocker-outside-the-set case cannot be recorded without manufacturing them on the real tracker.
- [ ] Tests cover: recursive descendant discovery; eligibility filtering; single-issue isolation; the repository-wide queue's ascending order; the topological sort keyed on authored order; prefix truncation; **precedence edge vs exclusion**; cycle detection; level computation; levels shrinking under transitive skips; the marker filter keeping bounce comments; the canonical digest being stable across key order.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir .sandcastle run check-types && pnpm --dir .sandcastle run test` green, and the suite still spawns nothing.

## Decisions to honour

- [Establish the GitHub issue-tree snapshot and eligibility query](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/390) — the snapshot's fields, normalization and the eligibility rules.
- [Settle batch ordering, stop conditions, and handoff semantics](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/394) — precedence edges, the sort, truncation, the transitive skip, the marker filter.
- [Define the Work scope contract across runner and workflows](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/392) §1–§2 — the module split and the kebab-case literals.
- [Decide the Work scope test and acceptance strategy](https://github.com/hadrysm/foldwise-voice/issues/396) — why literals and not fixtures.
